In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking soda, ground ginger, ground cinnamon, ground cloves, ground cardamom (if using), and salt.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing on low speed until just combined and a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.

Divide the dough into two equal portions. Shape each portion into a flat disk, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld and the dough to firm up.
Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line several baking sheets with parchment paper.

On a lightly floured surface or between two sheets of parchment paper, roll out one disk of chilled dough very thinly, about 1/16 to 1/8 inch (1.5-3mm) thick. The thinner the dough, the crispier the cookies will be.

Using cookie cutters of your choice (traditional shapes include stars, hearts, or simple rounds), cut out the ginger thins. Carefully transfer them to the prepared baking sheets, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) between cookies.
Bake for 6-8 minutes, or until the edges are lightly browned and the cookies are firm. Baking time may vary depending on thickness and oven.
Let the cookies cool on the baking sheets for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. Repeat with the remaining dough, gathering and re-rolling scraps as needed.
tips: For extra thin and crispy cookies, roll the dough directly between two sheets of parchment paper. This prevents sticking and makes transfer easier.
These ginger thins are delicious on their own, but also pair wonderfully with a cup of coffee, tea, or a glass of traditional Swedish glögg.
Store cooled ginger thins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks to maintain their crispness.

saffron-biscotti.title: Saffron Biscotti
saffron-biscotti.intro: Saffron Biscotti, with their beautiful golden hue, are a perfect treat to celebrate St. Lucia's Day, also known as Santa Lucia. The precious saffron spice symbolizes the light that St. Lucia brings during the darkest time of the year, offering a warm and comforting crunch alongside coffee or tea.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, steep the saffron threads in hot water or milk for 10 minutes to release their color and flavor.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla extract and the saffron mixture.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. Fold in the slivered almonds, if using. The dough will be stiff.
Divide the dough in half. On the prepared baking sheet, shape each half into a log, approximately 10-12 inches (25-30 cm) long and 2 inches (5 cm) wide. Leave space between logs.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the logs are firm to the touch and lightly golden.
Remove from the oven and let cool on the baking sheet for 10-15 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 300°F (150°C).
Carefully transfer the logs to a cutting board. Using a serrated knife, slice each log diagonally into 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) thick pieces.
Lay the sliced biscotti cut-side down back onto the baking sheet.
Bake for another 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the biscotti are golden brown and crisp.
Transfer the biscotti to a wire rack to cool completely. Store in an airtight container.
tips: For an extra festive touch, you can drizzle cooled biscotti with melted white chocolate.
Ensure the saffron steeps long enough to maximize its flavor and color.
Biscotti are meant to be hard; they are traditionally dipped in coffee, tea, or dessert wine.

julmust.title: Festive Julmust Serving
julmust.intro: Julmust is a beloved Swedish Christmas soft drink, often described as a spiced root beer, and it is an absolute staple during the holiday season in Sweden. While typically bought ready-made, serving it with a festive touch elevates the experience for St. Lucia's Day, a celebration of light and hope in the darkest part of winter. It's a non-alcoholic treat enjoyed by all ages alongside saffron buns and gingerbread cookies.
ingredients: 1 bottle (1.4 liters or 47 fl oz) Julmust, chilled
1 cinnamon stick, broken into smaller pieces
steps: Ensure your bottle of Julmust is thoroughly chilled in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours before serving.
Prepare your serving glasses. For an extra festive touch, you can lightly moisten the rim of each glass and dip it in granulated sugar (optional).
Place a few thin orange slices, a small piece of cinnamon stick, and one or two whole cloves (if using) into the bottom of each serving glass.
Carefully pour the chilled Julmust into the glasses over the spices and fruit, being mindful of its carbonation.
Garnish with a few fresh cranberries on top or a small sprig of rosemary for a wintery feel, if desired.
Serve immediately alongside traditional St. Lucia's Day treats like Lussebullar (saffron buns) and pepparkakor (gingerbread cookies).
tips: For a non-alcoholic 'mulled' aroma, gently warm a small amount (about 1/4 cup) of Julmust with the spices in a saucepan, then let it cool completely before adding it to the main chilled drink in the serving glasses. Do not boil, as it will lose carbonation.
Experiment with other spices like a star anise pod or a tiny slice of fresh ginger for a different aromatic twist.
Always serve Julmust well-chilled to best enjoy its complex flavors and effervescence; it loses much of its appeal when warm.

coffee.title: St. Lucia's Day Filter Coffee
coffee.intro: On St. Lucia's Day, December 13th, families traditionally wake early to celebrate with a special breakfast. Central to this festive morning is a warm cup of coffee, often served alongside saffron buns (lussekatter) and gingerbread cookies. This recipe guides you to brew a robust and comforting coffee, perfect for sharing during this beautiful Swedish tradition.
ingredients: 8 tablespoons (40g) medium-ground coffee beans (preferably freshly ground)
Optional: Sugar, milk, or cream to taste
steps: Measure the coffee grounds. For a standard brew, use 2 tablespoons (10g) of coffee for every 6 fluid ounces (180 mL) of water. For 4 cups (960 mL) of water, this means approximately 8 tablespoons (40g) of coffee.
If using whole beans, grind them to a medium consistency, similar to coarse sand, just before brewing.
Pour the measured filtered water into the reservoir of your drip coffee maker.
Place the coffee grounds into a clean filter in the coffee maker's basket.
Turn on the coffee maker and allow it to brew completely.
Once brewing is finished, carefully pour the hot coffee into mugs.
Serve immediately, offering sugar, milk, or cream on the side for guests to customize their cup.
tips: For the best flavor, use freshly roasted whole beans and grind them just before brewing.
Adjust the amount of coffee grounds to your preferred strength; add more for a bolder cup or less for a milder one.
Enjoy your St. Lucia's Day coffee with traditional Swedish saffron buns (lussekatter) and gingerbread cookies (pepparkakor) for a truly authentic experience.

red-pozole.title: Red Pozole
events: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe
red-pozole.intro: Red Pozole, or Pozole Rojo, is a hearty and flavorful Mexican stew traditionally made with hominy and pork, simmered in a rich, red chile broth. It is a beloved dish often prepared for special occasions and holidays, including the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, where families gather to celebrate with traditional foods that nourish both body and spirit.
ingredients: 3 pounds (1.4 kg) pork shoulder (Boston butt), cut into 2-inch (5 cm) cubes
1 teaspoon (5 g) dried oregano, preferably Mexican
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
12 cups (2.8 liters) water or chicken broth
3 (15-ounce / 425 g) cans white hominy, drained and rinsed
8 dried Guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried Ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
3-5 dried Chile de Arbol (optional, for heat), stemmed and seeded
steps: Place the pork shoulder in a large pot or Dutch oven. Add one half of the white onion, 3 cloves of garlic, bay leaves, 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) oregano, 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) cumin, 1 tablespoon (15 g) salt, and 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) black pepper.

Pour in 12 cups (2.8 liters) of water or chicken broth, ensuring the pork is fully submerged. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the pork is tender and easily shredded.

While the pork simmers, prepare the chile sauce. In a separate saucepan, combine the dried Guajillo, Ancho, and Arbol chiles. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, until the chiles are softened.

Carefully transfer the softened chiles to a blender. Add the remaining half of the white onion, 3 cloves of garlic, 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) oregano, 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) cumin, and 1 cup (240 ml) of the chile soaking liquid (or fresh water). Blend until completely smooth, adding more liquid if needed to achieve a pourable consistency.

Once the pork is tender, remove it from the pot and shred it using two forks. Discard the onion half, garlic cloves, and bay leaves from the cooking liquid. Strain the cooking liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, discarding any solids. This is your pork broth.

Return the shredded pork to the cleaned pot. Add the drained and rinsed hominy. Pour the blended chile sauce through a fine-mesh sieve directly into the pot with the pork and hominy, pressing on the solids to extract all the liquid. Discard the remaining pulp.

Add the strained pork broth back into the pot. Stir everything together. Bring the pozole to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Cook for another 30-45 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the hominy to fully absorb the broth. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.

Serve the Red Pozole hot in large bowls. Offer a variety of garnishes on the side, such as shredded cabbage, sliced radishes, diced white onion, chopped cilantro, and lime wedges, allowing each person to customize their bowl. Serve with tostadas or tortilla chips for dipping.
tips: For a richer flavor, toast the dried chiles lightly in a dry skillet for 1-2 minutes before soaking. Be careful not to burn them, as this can make the sauce bitter.
If you prefer a spicier pozole, you can add more Chile de Arbol or a pinch of cayenne pepper to the chile sauce.
Pozole tastes even better the next day! Make it ahead of time and gently reheat on the stovetop, adding a little water or broth if it has thickened too much.

lussekatter.title: Lussekatter (St. Lucia Buns)
lussekatter.intro: Lussekatter, or St. Lucia Buns, are traditional saffron-infused sweet buns enjoyed during Lussinatta (St. Lucia's Vigil) and St. Lucia's Day on December 13th in Sweden and other Nordic countries. Their distinctive S-shape and golden hue, from the saffron, symbolize light during the darkest time of the year, bringing warmth and cheer to the holiday season.
ingredients: 2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast (1 packet)
1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
4 1/2 to 5 cups (540-600 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1 large egg, beaten with 1 tablespoon water or milk (for egg wash)
steps: Gently warm the milk in a small saucepan until it is lukewarm (105-115°F / 40-46°C). Add the crushed saffron threads to the warm milk and let steep for 10 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the warm saffron milk, yeast, 1/4 cup (50 g) of the sugar, and salt. Let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
Stir in the melted butter and the 1 large egg (at room temperature) into the yeast mixture.
Gradually add the flour, about 1 cup (120 g) at a time, mixing until a soft dough forms. You may not need all 5 cups of flour; the dough should be slightly sticky but manageable.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, until smooth and elastic. If using a stand mixer, knead with the dough hook for 6-8 minutes.
Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and divide it into 24 equal pieces. On a lightly floured surface, roll each piece into a 8-10 inch (20-25 cm) rope.
Shape each rope into an 'S' by coiling both ends inward towards the center. Place two raisins in the center of each coil, one in each 'eye' of the 'S'.

Arrange the shaped buns on baking sheets lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel and let rise for another 30-45 minutes, or until puffy.
Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
Brush the risen buns with the egg wash.
Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until golden brown. Let cool on a wire rack before serving.
tips: For a more intense saffron flavor and color, steep the saffron in a tablespoon of spirits (like vodka or brandy) for 30 minutes before adding it to the warm milk.
Do not overheat the milk for the yeast; if it's too hot, it will kill the yeast. It should feel warm, not hot, to the touch.
Lussekatter are best enjoyed fresh, but can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or frozen for longer storage.

cheese-and-poblano-pepper-strip-tamales.title: Cheese and Poblano Pepper Strip Tamales
cheese-and-poblano-pepper-strip-tamales.dish: Cheese and Poblano Pepper Strip Tamales
events: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe
cheese-and-poblano-pepper-strip-tamales.intro: Tamales are a beloved and ancient Mesoamerican dish, deeply rooted in Mexican culture and often prepared for special occasions and holidays. For the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, families gather to honor the Virgin Mary with prayer, celebration, and a feast that frequently includes a variety of tamales, symbolizing community and tradition. These savory cheese and poblano tamales offer a comforting and flavorful addition to the festive table.
ingredients: 12 ounces (340g) Oaxaca cheese or Monterey Jack, cut into 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) strips
1 cup (226g) vegetable shortening or lard, at room temperature
4 cups (480g) masa harina for tamales (not regular masa harina for tortillas)
2 teaspoons (10g) fine sea salt, plus more to taste
3 1/2 to 4 cups (840-960ml) warm chicken or vegetable broth
steps: Soak the corn husks: Place dried corn husks in a large bowl or pot, cover completely with hot water, and weigh down with a plate to keep them submerged. Let them soak for at least 1 hour, or until pliable.

Prepare the poblano peppers: Roast the poblano peppers directly over an open flame (gas burner) or under a broiler until the skin is charred and blistered on all sides. Place the roasted peppers in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let steam for 10-15 minutes.
Peel and slice peppers: Once cooled, peel the skin from the peppers, remove the stems and seeds, and slice them into 1/4-inch (6mm) wide strips. Set aside.
Prepare the masa dough: In a large bowl, beat the shortening or lard with an electric mixer on medium-high speed until light and fluffy, about 3-5 minutes.
Combine dry ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk together the masa harina, baking powder, and salt.

Add masa to shortening: Gradually add the masa harina mixture to the beaten shortening, alternating with the warm broth, mixing until a soft, spreadable dough forms. The dough should be light and fluffy.
Test the masa: To test if the masa is ready, drop a small piece (about 1/2 teaspoon) into a glass of cold water; if it floats, it's ready. If not, beat for another minute or two and retest.

Assemble the tamales: Take a softened corn husk, wider end at the top. Spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa dough evenly over the wider part of the husk, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) clear at the top and sides.
Add filling: Place a few strips of poblano pepper and 1-2 strips of cheese in the center of the masa.
Fold the tamale: Fold one side of the husk over the filling, then the other side, overlapping slightly. Fold the narrow bottom end of the husk up towards the center. Leave the top open.
Repeat and arrange: Continue assembling tamales until all masa and filling are used.
Prepare for steaming: Arrange the tamales upright in a large steamer basket, open-end facing up. Do not pack them too tightly, as they need room to expand.

Steam the tamales: Place the steamer basket over a pot of simmering water, ensuring the water does not touch the tamales. Cover tightly and steam for 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes, or until the masa pulls away easily from the husk. Check water level periodically and add more hot water if needed.
Rest and serve: Let the tamales rest for 10-15 minutes off the heat before serving. Serve warm with your favorite salsa.
tips: For extra flavor, use the broth from cooking chicken or vegetables.
Ensure your masa dough is light and fluffy; this is key to tender tamales.
Don't overcrowd your steamer; steam in batches if necessary for even cooking.

green-tamales.title: Green Tamales (Tamales Verdes)
events: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe
green-tamales.intro: Green Tamales, or Tamales Verdes, are a festive and flavorful dish, deeply ingrained in Mexican culinary traditions, especially during celebrations. For the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, these savory parcels filled with tender chicken and a vibrant salsa verde are a beloved staple, symbolizing community and devotion as families gather to honor the Virgin of Guadalupe.
ingredients: 3-4 serrano peppers (or 2-3 jalapeños for milder), stems removed
4 cups (480g) masa harina for tamales (not regular masa flour)
1 1/2 cups (340g) lard or vegetable shortening, at room temperature
steps: Place corn husks in a large bowl or pot, cover with very hot water, and weigh down with a plate to keep them submerged. Let them soak for at least 1 hour, or until pliable.

While husks soak, prepare the salsa verde: Place tomatillos, serrano peppers, onion, and garlic in a medium saucepan. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 10-15 minutes, or until tomatillos are soft and have changed to a dull green color.

Drain the vegetables, reserving about 1/2 cup (120ml) of the cooking liquid. Transfer the cooked vegetables to a blender with the fresh cilantro and 1/4 cup (60ml) of the reserved cooking liquid. Blend until smooth, adding more liquid if needed to reach a pourable consistency.

Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Pour in the blended salsa verde (be careful, it may splatter). Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the salsa has thickened slightly and deepened in color. Season with salt to taste. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine the shredded cooked chicken with about 1 1/2 to 2 cups (360-480ml) of the prepared salsa verde, or enough to generously coat the chicken. Mix well and set aside.
In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment (or a large bowl with a hand mixer), beat the lard or shortening on medium-high speed until it is light and fluffy, about 3-5 minutes.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the masa harina, baking powder, and 2 teaspoons of salt.

Gradually add the masa harina mixture to the beaten lard, alternating with the warm chicken broth, mixing on low speed until just combined. Increase speed to medium and beat for 5-7 minutes, until the masa is light, fluffy, and resembles a soft dough. To test if the masa is ready, drop a small ball (about 1/2 teaspoon) into a cup of cold water; if it floats, it's ready. If it sinks, beat for a few more minutes and retest.
Drain the softened corn husks and pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel.

To assemble each tamale: Take one corn husk, wider end facing you. Spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa evenly over the wider part of the husk, leaving about 1 inch (2.5 cm) clear at the top and sides. The masa layer should be about 1/4 inch (0.6 cm) thick.
Place about 1-2 tablespoons of the chicken and salsa verde filling down the center of the masa.
Fold one long side of the husk over the filling, then fold the other long side over, overlapping slightly. Fold the narrow bottom end of the husk up towards the center. Leave the top open.
Repeat with the remaining masa, filling, and corn husks.

Set up a large steamer pot. Add water to just below the steamer basket. Arrange the tamales upright in the steamer basket, open-end facing up, packing them snugly. If you have extra corn husks, you can place them on top of the tamales to help trap steam.

Bring the water to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover tightly, and steam for 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes, or until the masa pulls away easily from the husk. Check water level periodically and add more hot water if needed.
Remove tamales from the steamer and let them rest for 10-15 minutes before serving. This allows them to firm up.
tips: For an extra layer of flavor, you can add a small piece of Oaxaca cheese or Monterey Jack cheese to the chicken filling.
Tamales freeze beautifully. Once cooled, wrap them individually in plastic wrap and then place them in a freezer-safe bag for up to 3 months. Reheat by steaming or microwaving.
The salsa verde can be made a day in advance to save time on assembly day. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

cinnamon-churros.title: Cinnamon Churros
events: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe
cinnamon-churros.intro: Cinnamon Churros are a beloved fried pastry, often enjoyed as a sweet treat during festive occasions in Mexico and among Mexican communities. On the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe, December 12th, these crispy, sugar-dusted delights are a popular indulgence, frequently paired with a warm cup of champurrado or Mexican hot chocolate as families gather to celebrate.
ingredients: 6 cups (1.4 L) vegetable oil, for frying
steps: In a medium saucepan, combine the water, butter, salt, and 1 tablespoon of sugar. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally until the butter is fully melted.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and immediately add all the flour at once. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms a ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Return the saucepan to low heat and continue to cook, stirring constantly for 1-2 minutes, to dry out the dough slightly. Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes.

Transfer the dough to a large mixing bowl. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well with a wooden spoon or electric mixer after each addition until fully incorporated and the dough is smooth and glossy.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large, deep pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F (175°C). Use a candy or deep-fry thermometer to monitor the temperature.
While the oil heats, prepare the cinnamon sugar coating: in a shallow dish, whisk together the 1/2 cup granulated sugar and ground cinnamon.
Spoon the churro dough into a piping bag fitted with a large star tip (like an Ateco 826 or 827).
Carefully pipe 4-6 inch (10-15 cm) strips of dough directly into the hot oil, using kitchen shears or a knife to cut the dough from the piping bag. Do not overcrowd the pot; fry in batches.
Fry the churros for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and cooked through. Use tongs or a slotted spoon to turn them as needed.
Remove the fried churros from the oil and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil for about 30 seconds.
While still warm, roll the churros in the cinnamon sugar mixture until evenly coated. Serve immediately.
tips: Maintain a consistent oil temperature of 350°F (175°C) for best results; if the oil is too cool, churros will be greasy, and if too hot, they will burn outside and be raw inside.
For extra flavor, you can add a teaspoon of vanilla extract to the dough along with the eggs.
Churros are best enjoyed fresh, but leftovers can be reheated briefly in a toaster oven or air fryer for a few minutes until crisp again.

guava-atole.title: Guava Atole
events: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe
guava-atole.intro: Guava Atole is a warm, comforting, and subtly sweet beverage, often enjoyed during the cooler months and especially cherished during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe. This traditional Mexican drink, thickened with masa harina, offers a delightful way to celebrate the holiday with its fragrant fruitiness, symbolizing warmth and community.
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) ripe guavas, fresh or frozen
1/2 cup (60 g) masa harina (corn flour for tortillas)
1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, or to taste
steps: If using fresh guavas, wash them thoroughly, trim the ends, and cut them into quarters. If using frozen, thaw them slightly.
Place the guava pieces in a blender with 1 cup (240 ml) of the milk. Blend until very smooth.
Strain the guava mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a medium saucepan, pressing on the solids with a spoon to extract as much pulp as possible. Discard any seeds and fibrous material.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the masa harina with 1 cup (240 ml) of the remaining milk until no lumps remain and it forms a smooth slurry.

Add the remaining 2 cups (480 ml) of milk, granulated sugar, and the cinnamon stick to the saucepan with the strained guava puree. Heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it just begins to simmer.
Slowly pour the masa harina slurry into the simmering guava mixture in the saucepan, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.

Continue to cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, for 10-15 minutes, or until the atole thickens to your desired consistency (it should be like a thin pudding or thick beverage). Be careful not to let it boil vigorously.
Remove the cinnamon stick before serving.
Serve hot, optionally garnished with a sprinkle of ground cinnamon.
tips: For a richer flavor, you can substitute half of the milk with evaporated milk.
Adjust the sugar to your preference; guavas vary in sweetness. Taste and add more if needed.
If the atole becomes too thick, whisk in a little more milk until it reaches the desired consistency.

bibingka.title: Bibingka (Traditional Filipino Baked Rice Cake)
bibingka.intro: Bibingka is a beloved Filipino rice cake, traditionally enjoyed after attending Simbang Gabi (dawn masses) during the Advent season, which includes Gaudete Sunday. This festive treat symbolizes warmth, community, and the joyful anticipation of Christmas, making it a perfect dish to share during this period of rejoicing.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter or margarine, melted, for brushing
1/2 cup (50 g) fresh grated coconut, for topping
steps: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). If using traditional bibingka molds, line them with softened banana leaves. If using a baking pan, line it with banana leaves, ensuring they extend slightly over the edges.
To soften banana leaves, carefully pass them over an open flame (like a gas burner) for a few seconds until they become pliable and change to a brighter green color. Be careful not to burn them.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the glutinous rice flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt until well combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs and coconut milk together until smooth.
Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, mixing continuously until a smooth, lump-free batter is formed. Do not overmix.
Pour the batter into the prepared banana leaf-lined molds or baking pan, filling them about two-thirds full.
Arrange the slices of salted duck egg and half of the grated cheddar cheese on top of the batter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean and the top is golden brown.
Once removed from the oven, immediately brush the tops of the bibingka generously with melted butter or margarine.
Sprinkle the remaining grated cheddar cheese and the fresh grated coconut over the warm bibingka.
Serve warm, directly from the molds or cut into wedges if using a baking pan.
tips: For an authentic smoky flavor, you can use a traditional clay oven (pugon) or a grill with a lid and hot coals on top and bottom.
If you don't have salted duck eggs, you can omit them or use regular hard-boiled eggs for a milder flavor.
Experiment with other toppings like latik (coconut milk curds) or a drizzle of condensed milk for added sweetness.

puto-bumbong.title: Puto Bumbong
puto-bumbong.intro: Puto Bumbong is a beloved Filipino steamed rice cake, distinctively purple and traditionally cooked in bamboo tubes. It's a quintessential treat during the Christmas season in the Philippines, especially enjoyed after attending Simbang Gabi (dawn masses), which includes Gaudete Sunday. Its warm, slightly sweet, and chewy texture, topped with butter, shredded coconut, and muscovado sugar, makes it a comforting and festive holiday staple.
ingredients: 2 cups (240 g) glutinous rice flour (preferably purple glutinous rice flour or mixed with 1/2 tsp ube powder for color)
2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter or margarine, softened
1/4 cup (50 g) muscovado sugar (or dark brown sugar)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the glutinous rice flour (and ube powder, if using) and salt. Gradually add water, mixing until a soft, pliable dough forms. The dough should be moist but not sticky.
Divide the dough into small, log-like pieces, about 2-3 inches (5-7.5 cm) long and 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) thick.
Prepare your steamer. If you have a traditional puto bumbong steamer with bamboo tubes, use that. Otherwise, line a regular steamer basket with banana leaves or parchment paper.
Arrange the dough pieces in the prepared steamer, ensuring they are not overcrowded. Steam for 5-7 minutes, or until they are soft, chewy, and cooked through.
Carefully remove the steamed puto bumbong from the steamer.
While still hot, brush each piece generously with softened butter or margarine.
Arrange the puto bumbong on a plate. Sprinkle generously with grated coconut and muscovado sugar.
Serve immediately and enjoy warm.
tips: For an authentic purple color, look for 'pirurutong' glutinous rice flour or add a small amount of ube powder to regular glutinous rice flour.
If you don't have a bamboo steamer, a regular steamer basket lined with banana leaves or parchment paper works well. Banana leaves impart a subtle aroma.
Adjust the amount of butter, coconut, and sugar to your personal preference. Some also like a drizzle of condensed milk for extra sweetness.

crispy-tacos.title: Crispy Chicken Tacos for the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe
events: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe
crispy-tacos.intro: Crispy Tacos, known as Tacos Dorados in Mexico, are a beloved festive dish, often gracing tables during celebrations like the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th. These golden, crunchy tacos, typically filled with savory shredded chicken or potato, are a comforting and joyful addition to any family gathering, symbolizing the warmth and tradition of Mexican cuisine.
ingredients: 1 pound (450g) boneless, skinless chicken breasts or thighs
1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
1/2 teaspoon black pepper, plus more to taste
3-4 cups (700-950 ml) vegetable oil, for frying
1 head iceberg or romaine lettuce, shredded
1 cup (115g) crumbled queso fresco or cotija cheese
1 cup (240 ml) salsa roja or verde
1/2 cup (120 ml) Mexican crema or sour cream
steps: Place chicken, onion quarters, and smashed garlic cloves in a medium pot. Cover with water by about 1 inch (2.5 cm). Add 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and easily shreddable.
Remove chicken from the pot, reserving about 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the cooking liquid. Let chicken cool slightly, then shred it using two forks.
In a bowl, combine the shredded chicken with the ground cumin, dried oregano, and 2-3 tablespoons of the reserved cooking liquid. Mix well and taste, adjusting salt and pepper if needed.

Warm the corn tortillas to make them pliable. You can do this by heating them briefly in a microwave (stacked, covered with a damp paper towel, for 30-60 seconds) or on a dry griddle for 15-20 seconds per side.
Place about 1-2 tablespoons of the shredded chicken filling near one edge of each warm tortilla. Roll the tortilla tightly into a cylinder.
If desired, secure each rolled taco with a toothpick to prevent it from unraveling during frying. (This step is optional, as they often stay rolled once fried).

In a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or Dutch oven, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat until it reaches 350-375°F (175-190°C). If you don't have a thermometer, a small piece of tortilla should sizzle immediately when dropped in.
Carefully place 3-4 rolled tacos into the hot oil, seam-side down first. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy.
Remove fried tacos with tongs and place them on a wire rack set over a baking sheet lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Repeat with the remaining tacos, ensuring the oil temperature stays consistent.

Remove any toothpicks before serving. Arrange the crispy tacos on a platter and top generously with shredded lettuce, crumbled queso fresco, salsa roja or verde, and a drizzle of Mexican crema or sour cream.
tips: For a vegetarian option, replace chicken with seasoned mashed potatoes or black beans.
To make ahead, prepare the chicken filling and shred the lettuce. Fry the tacos just before serving for maximum crispiness.
Serve with a side of refried beans and Mexican rice for a complete festive meal.

fruit-punch.title: Gaudete Sunday Festive Fruit Punch
fruit-punch.intro: Gaudete Sunday, the third Sunday of Advent, is a time of joyful anticipation, marked by rose vestments and a spirit of rejoicing. This festive fruit punch, with its vibrant colors and sweet-tart flavors, perfectly embodies the celebratory mood of the day, offering a refreshing treat for family and friends.
ingredients: 1/2 cup (120 mL) fresh lime juice, chilled
2 liters (about 8.5 cups) ginger ale or sparkling cider, chilled
1 cup (150 g) fresh cranberries, for garnish
Optional: Ice ring or extra ice cubes
steps: In a large punch bowl, combine the chilled cranberry juice, orange juice, pineapple juice, and fresh lime juice.
Stir gently to combine all the juices.
Just before serving, slowly pour in the chilled ginger ale or sparkling cider.
Add the fresh cranberries and orange slices to the punch bowl for garnish.
Serve immediately over ice, or with an ice ring to keep it cold without diluting.
tips: For an extra festive touch, freeze some cranberries and orange slices in an ice ring or individual ice cubes.
Adjust the sweetness by adding a tablespoon or two of simple syrup if you prefer a sweeter punch.
You can prepare the juice mixture ahead of time and store it in the refrigerator, adding the sparkling beverage and garnishes just before serving.

bunuelos-de-viento.title: Buñuelos de Viento
events: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe
bunuelos-de-viento.intro: Buñuelos de Viento are light, airy fried dough pastries, a beloved sweet treat traditionally enjoyed during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th. This significant religious holiday in Mexico is a time for celebration, family gatherings, and special foods, with these delicate, sugar-dusted fritters symbolizing joy and festivity.
ingredients: 1 cup (240 ml) water or whole milk
4-6 cups (950-1400 ml) vegetable oil, for frying
1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, for coating
1 tablespoon (15 g) ground cinnamon, for coating
steps: In a medium saucepan, combine the water (or milk), butter, salt, and 1 tablespoon of sugar. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally to melt the butter.

Remove the saucepan from the heat and immediately add the all-purpose flour all at once. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until the mixture forms a smooth ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Return the pan to low heat and continue to cook, stirring constantly for 1-2 minutes, to dry out the dough slightly. This step is crucial for a light texture.
Transfer the dough to a large mixing bowl. Let it cool for 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it's warm but not hot to the touch.

Add the eggs one at a time, beating well with an electric mixer or a sturdy spoon after each addition, until fully incorporated and the dough is smooth and glossy. The dough will look curdled at first, but keep mixing until it comes together.
Stir in the vanilla extract until combined.
In a deep pot or Dutch oven, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat to 350-375°F (175-190°C). If using a buñuelo mold, submerge it in the hot oil for a few minutes to heat it thoroughly.

For frying with a mold: Dip the hot mold into the buñuelo batter, ensuring the batter adheres to the mold without covering the top edge. Immediately transfer the mold back into the hot oil. The buñuelo should release from the mold after about 30-60 seconds. If it doesn't, gently nudge it off with tongs or a fork.
For frying without a mold: Drop rounded tablespoons of batter directly into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Fry the buñuelos for 2-4 minutes per side, or until they are golden brown and puffed. Use tongs or a slotted spoon to turn them as needed.
Carefully remove the fried buñuelos from the oil and place them on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
In a shallow dish, combine the 1/2 cup of granulated sugar and ground cinnamon. While the buñuelos are still warm, toss them gently in the cinnamon sugar mixture until evenly coated.
Serve immediately and enjoy the festive treat!
tips: Maintain the oil temperature: Use a thermometer to keep the oil between 350-375°F (175-190°C) for best results. Too cool, and they'll be greasy; too hot, and they'll burn.
Don't overcrowd the pot: Fry buñuelos in small batches to prevent the oil temperature from dropping too much and to ensure even cooking.
Serve with a dipping sauce: Buñuelos are delicious on their own, but can also be served with a side of warm piloncillo syrup or a cup of traditional Mexican hot chocolate or atole.

potato-latkes.title: Classic Hanukkah Potato Latkes
potato-latkes.intro: Potato Latkes are crispy, savory pancakes traditionally enjoyed during the Jewish holiday of Hanukkah, the Festival of Lights. Their preparation involves frying in oil, symbolizing the miracle of the oil that burned for eight days in the Temple. Served hot, they are a beloved centerpiece of Hanukkah celebrations.
ingredients: 2 lbs (900g) Russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled
1/4 cup (30g) all-purpose flour or matzo meal
3-4 cups (700-950ml) vegetable oil, canola oil, or grapeseed oil, for frying
Applesauce and sour cream, for serving (optional)
steps: Grate the potatoes using the large holes of a box grater or a food processor. Immediately transfer the grated potatoes to a large bowl of cold water to prevent browning.
Grate the onion using the large holes of a box grater or a food processor.
Drain the grated potatoes thoroughly. Place them in a clean kitchen towel or several layers of cheesecloth and wring out as much liquid as possible. This step is crucial for crispy latkes.
In a large bowl, combine the well-drained grated potatoes, grated onion, beaten eggs, flour (or matzo meal), salt, and pepper. Mix until just combined.
Heat about 1/2 inch (1.25 cm) of oil in a large, heavy-bottomed skillet (cast iron works well) over medium-high heat until shimmering, about 350°F (175°C).
Carefully drop spoonfuls (about 2 tablespoons each) of the potato mixture into the hot oil, flattening them slightly with the back of the spoon to form thin pancakes. Do not overcrowd the skillet.
Fry for 3-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy. Adjust heat as needed to prevent burning.
Remove the latkes from the skillet with a slotted spoon or spatula and place them on a wire rack set over a baking sheet lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve immediately with applesauce and sour cream, if desired.
tips: For extra crispy latkes, ensure you squeeze out as much liquid as possible from the grated potatoes and onions.
Keep fried latkes warm in a single layer on a baking sheet in a 200°F (95°C) oven while you finish frying the rest.
For a slightly different flavor, add a pinch of garlic powder or a tablespoon of chopped fresh chives to the potato mixture.

mole-poblano-with-rice.title: Mole Poblano with Rice
events: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe
mole-poblano-with-rice.intro: Mole Poblano is a rich, complex sauce, considered one of Mexico's national dishes. For the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, it is a beloved centerpiece, symbolizing celebration and gratitude, often served after mass as families gather to honor the Virgin Mary. Its deep, layered flavors make it a fitting dish for such a significant and joyous occasion.
ingredients: 3-4 pounds (1.4-1.8 kg) bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, breasts)
Salt to taste (for chicken and mole)
4 ancho chiles (dried poblano peppers), stemmed and seeded
3 mulato chiles (dried poblano peppers), stemmed and seeded
3 pasilla chiles (dried pasilla negro peppers), stemmed and seeded
1 chipotle chile (dried smoked jalapeño), stemmed and seeded (optional, for heat)
2 tablespoons (30 ml) sesame seeds, plus more for garnish
1 (3-inch / 7.5 cm) cinnamon stick, preferably Mexican canela
1/2 medium white onion, roughly chopped (for mole)
2 Roma tomatoes (about 8 oz / 225 g), roughly chopped
2 tomatillos (about 4 oz / 115 g), husked and roughly chopped
1/2 plantain, ripe (yellow with black spots), peeled and sliced
1 slice stale bread or 1 stale corn tortilla
1 ounce (28 g) Mexican chocolate (unsweetened or semi-sweet), broken into pieces
1/4 cup (60 ml) lard or vegetable oil, plus 1 tablespoon (15 ml) for rice
4-6 cups (960 ml - 1.4 L) chicken broth, divided (from cooking chicken)
2 cups (400 g) long-grain white rice, rinsed
1/4 cup (35 g) finely diced white onion (for rice)
3 cups (720 ml) chicken broth or water (for rice)
1 tablespoon (15 g) tomato paste (optional, for color in rice)
steps: Prepare the Chicken: Place chicken pieces, 1/2 quartered onion, 2 smashed garlic cloves, bay leaf, and a generous pinch of salt in a large pot. Cover with water by about 1 inch (2.5 cm). Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through. Remove chicken, let cool slightly, then shred or cut into serving pieces. Strain the broth and reserve 4-6 cups (960 ml - 1.4 L) for the mole and rice.

Prepare the Chiles: While chicken cooks, toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30-60 seconds per side, until fragrant and slightly pliable (do not burn). Transfer to a bowl, cover with hot water, and let rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft. Drain, reserving a little soaking liquid if needed for blending.
Toast Nuts and Seeds: In the same dry skillet, toast peanuts, almonds, sesame seeds, and pumpkin seeds separately until lightly golden and fragrant. Set aside.

Fry Aromatics and Spices: Heat 1/4 cup (60 ml) lard or oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the 1/2 roughly chopped onion, 4 peeled garlic cloves, tomatoes, tomatillos, plantain, and stale bread/tortilla. Fry until softened and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes. Add the cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, anise seeds, oregano, and cumin; cook for another minute until fragrant.

Blend the Mole Paste: Transfer the fried aromatics, spices, toasted nuts, and rehydrated chiles to a blender. Add 2 cups (480 ml) of the reserved chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. This may take several minutes and you might need to do it in batches. For an extra smooth mole, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids with a spoon.

Cook the Mole: In the same pot (cleaned if necessary), heat another tablespoon of lard or oil over medium heat. Pour in the blended mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 20-30 minutes. The mole will darken in color, thicken, and the oil will separate slightly. This step is crucial for developing deep flavor.

Simmer the Mole: Gradually stir in the remaining 2-4 cups (480 ml - 960 ml) of chicken broth, a little at a time, until the mole reaches your desired consistency (it should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon). Add the Mexican chocolate and stir until melted and fully incorporated. Add the optional sugar if needed to balance the flavors. Season with salt to taste. Reduce heat to low and simmer for at least 30-60 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking, allowing the flavors to meld.

Prepare the Rice: While the mole simmers, heat 1 tablespoon (15 ml) vegetable oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the rinsed rice and sauté for 3-5 minutes until lightly golden. Add the 1/4 cup (35 g) finely diced onion and minced garlic; sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.

Cook the Rice: Stir in 3 cups (720 ml) chicken broth (or water), optional tomato paste, and salt to taste. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes before fluffing with a fork.

Serve: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering mole and heat through for 5-10 minutes. Serve the Mole Poblano over chicken, accompanied by the Mexican rice. Garnish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds.
tips: Make Ahead: Mole poblano tastes even better the next day! Prepare the mole sauce a day or two in advance and gently reheat, adding a little more broth if needed to adjust consistency.
Spice Level: Adjust the number of chipotle chiles (or omit) based on your preferred spice level. For a milder mole, remove more seeds and veins from the chiles.
Authenticity: Using Mexican chocolate (often found in disc or tablet form) and Mexican oregano will give your mole a more authentic flavor profile.

bimuelos.title: Bimuelos (Hanukkah Honey Fritters)
bimuelos.intro: Bimuelos are light, airy fried dough fritters, often soaked in a sweet syrup, traditionally enjoyed by Sephardic Jews during Hanukkah. Their preparation involves frying in oil, symbolizing the miracle of the oil that lasted eight days in the Temple. They are a delightful, sweet treat perfect for celebrating the Festival of Lights.
steps: In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and 1 tablespoon granulated sugar. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
Add the flour and salt to the yeast mixture. Mix until a soft, sticky dough forms; do not overmix.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
While the dough rises, prepare the syrup: combine 1/2 cup water, honey, 1/4 cup granulated sugar, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel (if using) in a small saucepan.
Bring the syrup mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened. Remove from heat, discard cinnamon and lemon peel, and let cool completely.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or deep fryer, heat about 3-4 inches (7-10 cm) of vegetable oil to 350°F (175°C).
Dip your fingers in a little oil or water to prevent sticking. Pinch off small pieces of dough (about 1 tablespoon each) and carefully drop them into the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Fry the bimuelos for 2-3 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until they are golden brown and puffed.
Remove the fried bimuelos with a slotted spoon and place them on a wire rack set over paper towels to drain excess oil.
While still warm, dip each bimuelo into the cooled honey syrup, ensuring it's fully coated.
Arrange on a platter and serve immediately.
tips: For extra flavor, you can add a pinch of ground cinnamon or orange zest to the dough.
Ensure the oil temperature remains consistent for even cooking; use a thermometer if possible.
Bimuelos are best enjoyed fresh, but leftovers can be gently reheated in a warm oven.

macarons.title: Rose Raspberry Macarons for Gaudete Sunday
macarons.intro: Gaudete Sunday, the third Sunday of Advent, is a joyful pause in the solemn Advent season, marked by the lighting of the pink candle and rose-colored vestments. These delicate Rose Raspberry Macarons, with their festive pink hue and sweet filling, offer a perfect way to celebrate this day of rejoicing with a special, homemade treat.
ingredients: 100 g (1 cup) almond flour, finely ground
70 g (about 2 large) egg whites, aged at room temperature for a few hours or overnight
1/4 cup (60 g) good quality raspberry jam
steps: Prepare two baking sheets by lining them with parchment paper or silicone mats. If desired, draw 1.5-inch (4 cm) circles on the parchment paper, spaced about 1 inch (2.5 cm) apart.
In a medium bowl, sift together the almond flour and powdered sugar. Discard any large pieces of almond that don't pass through the sieve. Sift again into a clean bowl to ensure a very fine mixture.

In a separate large, clean bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the egg whites with a pinch of salt on medium speed until foamy. Gradually add the granulated sugar, one tablespoon at a time, continuing to beat on high speed until the meringue is glossy and forms stiff peaks. Add the pink gel food coloring and beat until fully incorporated.

Add about one-third of the dry ingredients to the meringue. Using a rubber spatula, gently fold them in. Add the remaining dry ingredients in two more additions, folding until just combined. Continue to fold, scraping down the sides of the bowl, until the batter flows like lava from your spatula and forms a 'figure eight' when dropped back into the bowl (this is called 'macaronage'). Be careful not to overmix.
Transfer the macaron batter to a piping bag fitted with a round tip (e.g., Wilton 1A or Ateco 806).
Pipe uniform circles onto the prepared baking sheets, following your drawn guides if using. Hold the piping bag straight up and pipe from the center, lifting straight up when done.
Firmly tap the baking sheets on the counter 2-3 times to release any trapped air bubbles. Use a toothpick to pop any remaining bubbles on the surface of the shells.
Let the piped macarons rest at room temperature for 1 to 2 hours, or until a skin forms on top and they are no longer sticky to the touch. This step is crucial for developing the 'feet'.
Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C) during the last 30 minutes of the resting period.

Bake one tray at a time for 12-15 minutes, or until the 'feet' have formed and the shells are firm and don't wobble when gently touched. If they brown too quickly, you can slightly reduce the oven temperature.
Carefully remove the baking sheets from the oven and let the macaron shells cool completely on the sheets before attempting to peel them off. This prevents breakage.

While the shells cool, prepare the filling: In a medium bowl, beat the softened butter with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Gradually add the powdered sugar, beating until smooth. Beat in the vanilla extract and 1 tablespoon of milk or cream. Add more milk/cream if needed to reach a spreadable consistency. Fold in the raspberry jam until just combined.

Once the macaron shells are completely cool, match them up by size. Pipe or spread a dollop of raspberry buttercream onto the flat side of one shell, then gently top with a matching shell to create a sandwich. Repeat with the remaining shells.

Store the assembled macarons in an airtight container in the refrigerator for at least 24 hours before serving for the best flavor and texture. Let them come to room temperature for about 15-20 minutes before enjoying.
tips: Aged egg whites (separated a day or two in advance and left in a covered container at room temperature) whip up better and create a more stable meringue.
Do not overmix the macaron batter during the 'macaronage' stage; it should flow slowly, not run. Overmixing leads to flat macarons without 'feet'.
Oven temperature can vary significantly. It's recommended to use an oven thermometer to ensure accuracy, as consistent heat is key for macaron success.

eggs.title: Ostara Naturally Dyed Eggs
eggs.intro: Eggs are a quintessential symbol of new life, fertility, and rebirth, making them central to Spring Equinox (Ostara) celebrations. This recipe guides you through creating beautiful, naturally dyed eggs, a joyful and traditional way to welcome the spring and adorn your Ostara altar or table. These vibrant eggs represent the awakening of nature and the promise of new beginnings.
ingredients: 4 cups (960 ml) water, plus more for dye baths
2 tablespoons (30 ml) white vinegar, per dye bath
For Yellow/Orange: 2 cups (approx. 50 g) yellow onion skins
For Blue/Purple: 1/2 head (approx. 250 g) red cabbage, chopped
For Golden Yellow: 2 tablespoons (30 ml) ground turmeric
For Brown: 1/2 cup (120 ml) strong brewed coffee grounds or instant coffee
Optional: 1 teaspoon (5 ml) vegetable oil, for shine
steps: Gently place eggs in a single layer in a large saucepan. Cover with at least 1 inch (2.5 cm) of cold water.
Bring water to a rolling boil over high heat. Once boiling, immediately remove the pan from heat, cover, and let stand for 12-15 minutes for hard-boiled eggs.

While eggs are cooking, prepare your dye baths. For each color, combine the dye ingredient (onion skins, red cabbage, turmeric, or coffee) with 2 cups (480 ml) of water and 2 tablespoons (30 ml) white vinegar in separate small saucepans.

Bring each dye mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes to extract the color. Strain the solids from each dye bath, reserving the colored liquid in separate heatproof bowls or jars.
Carefully transfer the hard-boiled eggs to an ice bath or run under cold water to stop the cooking process and cool them completely. This prevents a green ring around the yolk.
Once eggs are cool, gently place them into the prepared dye baths. Ensure eggs are fully submerged. For deeper colors, you may need to add more dye liquid or turn the eggs periodically.
Allow eggs to soak in the dye for at least 2 hours for pastel shades, or overnight in the refrigerator for more vibrant, deeper colors.
Once desired color is achieved, carefully remove eggs from the dye baths using a slotted spoon and place them on a wire rack set over paper towels to dry completely.
For an optional shine, once dry, gently rub each egg with a tiny amount of vegetable oil using a paper towel.
tips: Experiment with other natural dyes like beet juice for pink, spinach for light green, or paprika for orange-red.
For speckled eggs, before dyeing, wrap eggs in onion skins or small leaves and secure with cheesecloth or an old nylon stocking.
Store dyed eggs in the refrigerator and consume within one week, as they are hard-boiled.

braised-brisket.title: Classic Hanukkah Braised Brisket
braised-brisket.intro: Braised brisket is a beloved centerpiece for many Hanukkah celebrations, symbolizing warmth, family, and abundance during the Festival of Lights. Its slow-cooked tenderness and rich, savory gravy make it a comforting and deeply flavorful dish, perfect for gathering loved ones around the holiday table.
ingredients: 1 (4-5 pound / 1.8-2.3 kg) beef brisket, flat cut, trimmed of excess hard fat
2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil or vegetable oil
4 carrots, peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) chunks
3 celery stalks, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) chunks
1 cup (240 ml) dry red wine (such as Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon)
3 cups (720 ml) beef broth or stock
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
1/2 teaspoon black pepper, freshly ground, plus more to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
Pat the brisket dry thoroughly with paper towels. Season generously all over with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.

Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear the brisket fat-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply browned and a crust forms. Flip and sear the other side for another 5-7 minutes. Remove brisket from the pot and set aside.

Add the sliced onions, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes. Add the minced garlic and tomato paste, and cook for another 2 minutes, stirring constantly until fragrant.
Pour in the red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon. Let it simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Return the brisket to the pot, placing it fat-side up on top of the vegetables. Pour in the beef broth and water. Add the bay leaves and dried thyme.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer on the stovetop. Cover the Dutch oven tightly with its lid.
Transfer the Dutch oven to the preheated oven and braise for 3 to 3.5 hours, or until the brisket is fork-tender. The exact time will depend on the thickness of your brisket.

Remove the Dutch oven from the oven. Carefully transfer the brisket to a cutting board, tent with foil, and let it rest for at least 15-20 minutes before slicing. This resting period is crucial for juicy meat.

While the brisket rests, skim any excess fat from the surface of the braising liquid. You can serve the vegetables and sauce as is, or for a smoother sauce, strain the liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing on the solids to extract all the flavor. Discard the solids, then return the sauce to the pot and simmer briefly to reduce if desired. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Slice the brisket against the grain into 1/4-inch (0.6 cm) thick slices. Arrange on a platter, spoon the sauce and vegetables over the top, and garnish with fresh parsley if using. Serve hot.
tips: Make Ahead: Brisket is even better the next day! Prepare it a day in advance, let it cool completely, then refrigerate. The next day, remove the solidified fat from the top, slice the cold brisket, and reheat gently in the sauce.
Slicing Technique: Always slice brisket against the grain. This shortens the muscle fibers, making the meat much more tender and easier to chew.
Flavor Boost: For a touch of sweetness, add 1/4 cup (60 ml) of dried prunes or dried apricots along with the liquids before braising.

sufganiyot.title: Sufganiyot (Hanukkah Jelly Doughnuts)
sufganiyot.intro: Sufganiyot are delightful, deep-fried jelly doughnuts traditionally enjoyed during Hanukkah, the Jewish Festival of Lights. Their preparation, involving frying in oil, symbolizes and celebrates the miracle of the oil that lasted eight days in the Temple of Jerusalem. These fluffy, sweet treats are a joyous centerpiece for any Hanukkah celebration.
ingredients: 2 1/4 teaspoons (7g) active dry yeast (one standard packet)
2 1/2 cups (300g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1/4 cup (56g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
4-6 cups (about 1-1.5 liters) vegetable oil, for frying
1 cup (240g) strawberry or raspberry jam, for filling
steps: In a small bowl, combine the warm milk, 1 teaspoon of granulated sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, remaining 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar, and salt.
Add the proofed yeast mixture, eggs, and melted butter to the dry ingredients. Mix with a wooden spoon or stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes, or use a stand mixer for 5-7 minutes, until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky.

Lightly grease a clean bowl with a little oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
Once risen, gently punch down the dough. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and roll it out to about 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) thickness.

Using a 2.5-3 inch (6-7.5 cm) round cookie cutter or a drinking glass, cut out circles of dough. Gather and re-roll scraps once to cut out more doughnuts. Place the cut doughnuts on a parchment-lined baking sheet, leaving some space between them.
Cover the doughnuts loosely with plastic wrap or a clean towel and let them rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.

While the doughnuts are rising for the second time, heat the vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat to 350°F (175°C). Use a deep-fry thermometer to monitor the temperature.
Carefully lower 2-3 doughnuts into the hot oil, being careful not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Using a slotted spoon or spider, remove the fried doughnuts and place them on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.

Once slightly cooled but still warm, fill the doughnuts. Use a piping bag fitted with a long, thin nozzle (or a clean pastry bag with a small corner snipped off) to inject about 1 tablespoon of jam into the side of each doughnut.
Dust generously with powdered sugar before serving. Sufganiyot are best enjoyed warm on the day they are made.
tips: Maintaining the oil temperature is crucial; if it's too low, the doughnuts will be greasy, and if too high, they'll brown too quickly on the outside and be raw inside.
For a richer flavor, you can add a teaspoon of vanilla extract or a pinch of nutmeg to the dough.
If you don't have a piping bag, you can make a small incision in the side of the doughnut with a knife and carefully spoon in the jam.

citrus.title: Spring Equinox Citrus Salad
citrus.intro: This vibrant Citrus Salad celebrates the balance and renewal of the Spring Equinox, or Ostara. Featuring a medley of bright, juicy citrus fruits and a refreshing honey-mint dressing, it symbolizes the returning light and fresh energy of spring. It's a perfect light and invigorating dish to share as nature awakens.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon (15ml) finely chopped fresh Mint leaves
steps: Prepare the citrus fruits: Using a sharp knife, slice off the top and bottom of each orange and grapefruit.
Stand each fruit on one of its cut ends. Carefully slice downwards, following the curve of the fruit, to remove all the peel and white pith.
Working over a bowl to catch the juices, carefully slice between the membranes to release individual citrus segments. Discard any seeds.
Place the segmented citrus fruits in a large serving bowl.
For the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together the lime juice, honey, finely chopped mint leaves, and a pinch of salt until well combined.
Pour the dressing over the citrus segments. Gently toss to coat.
If using, sprinkle the pomegranate seeds over the salad just before serving.
Serve immediately or chill for up to 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
tips: For an extra floral note, add 1/4 teaspoon (1.25ml) of orange blossom water to the dressing.
Experiment with different citrus varieties like Cara Cara oranges or pomelos for varied color and flavor.
Garnish with a few extra fresh mint leaves for a beautiful presentation.

tender-vegetables.title: Tender Spring Vegetables with Lemon-Herb Dressing
tender-vegetables.intro: This vibrant dish celebrates the awakening of nature and the fresh bounty of spring, making it a perfect centerpiece for your Ostara or Spring Equinox feast. It highlights the delicate flavors and textures of early season vegetables, symbolizing renewal and growth as the earth comes back to life. Light, refreshing, and full of color, it's a wonderful way to honor the season's promise.
ingredients: 1 pound (450g) fresh asparagus, tough ends trimmed
1 cup (150g) baby carrots, scrubbed or peeled
6-8 small radishes, thinly sliced or halved
1/2 teaspoon sea salt, or to taste
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, or to taste
steps: Prepare a large bowl of ice water and set it aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add the baby carrots to the boiling water and cook for 2-3 minutes, until tender-crisp. Using a slotted spoon, immediately transfer them to the ice bath to stop the cooking.
Add the asparagus spears to the same boiling water and cook for 2-3 minutes, until bright green and tender-crisp. Transfer them to the ice bath.
Add the snap peas to the boiling water and cook for 1-2 minutes, until bright green and crisp-tender. Transfer them to the ice bath.
Once all vegetables are cooled, drain them thoroughly from the ice water and pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel or paper towels. Place them in a large serving bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, fresh dill, fresh parsley, lemon zest (if using), salt, and pepper until well combined.
Pour the dressing over the blanched vegetables and add the sliced radishes. Gently toss to coat all the vegetables evenly.
Serve immediately, or at room temperature.
tips: Feel free to substitute or add other tender spring vegetables like green beans, shelled peas, or thinly sliced zucchini.
For an extra touch of richness, sprinkle with toasted slivered almonds or crumbled feta cheese just before serving.
Ensure vegetables are thoroughly dried after the ice bath; this helps the dressing adhere better and prevents a watery dish.

herbs.title: Spring Herb and Feta Frittata
herbs.intro: This vibrant Spring Herb and Feta Frittata celebrates the fresh growth of Ostara, the Spring Equinox. Bursting with the flavors of new herbs and rich eggs, it's a perfect dish to welcome the season's renewal and share with loved ones during a celebratory brunch or light meal.
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk or cream, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper until well combined and slightly frothy.
Heat the olive oil in a 10-inch (25 cm) oven-safe, non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped shallot and cook until softened, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped spinach and cook until just wilted, about 1-2 minutes. Remove the skillet from the heat.
Gently stir in the fresh parsley, chives, dill, and mint into the egg mixture.
Pour the egg and herb mixture evenly over the vegetables in the skillet. Sprinkle the crumbled feta cheese over the top.
Cook on the stovetop over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes, or until the edges begin to set and pull away from the sides of the pan.
Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for 15-18 minutes, or until the frittata is puffed and set in the center.
Let the frittata rest for 5 minutes before slicing into wedges and serving.
tips: Feel free to experiment with other spring herbs like tarragon or basil.
For added texture, you can include thinly sliced asparagus or green onions.
Serve warm or at room temperature, perhaps with a side of crusty bread or a light green salad.

roast-pork.title: Saturnalia Roast Pork
roast-pork.intro: This succulent roast pork, seasoned with aromatic herbs and spices, is a centerpiece for any Saturnalia feast. As the Roman festival of Saturnalia celebrated the winter solstice with feasting, gift-giving, and revelry, a grand roast like this would have been a highlight of the communal meals, symbolizing abundance and good cheer.
ingredients: 3-4 pounds (1.4-1.8 kg) boneless pork loin roast
1 tablespoon fresh fennel seeds, crushed (or 1 teaspoon ground fennel)
1/2 cup (120 ml) dry white wine or chicken broth
steps: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
Pat the pork loin roast dry with paper towels. If there is a fat cap, you can score it lightly in a crosshatch pattern, being careful not to cut into the meat.
In a small bowl, combine the minced garlic, chopped rosemary, crushed fennel seeds, sea salt, and black pepper. Stir in the olive oil to form a paste.
Rub the herb and spice paste generously all over the pork loin roast, ensuring it is evenly coated.
Place the seasoned pork roast in a roasting pan. Pour the white wine or chicken broth into the bottom of the pan, and add the bay leaves if using.

Roast for 1 hour 30 minutes to 1 hour 45 minutes, or until an internal temperature of 145°F (63°C) is reached in the thickest part of the roast. For a crispier exterior, you can increase the oven temperature to 400°F (200°C) for the last 15 minutes.

Once cooked, remove the pork from the oven, transfer it to a cutting board, and tent loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 15-20 minutes before slicing. This allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in a more tender and flavorful roast.
Slice the roast pork against the grain into 1/2-inch (1.2 cm) thick pieces. Serve immediately with any pan juices.
tips: For extra flavor, you can sear the pork roast in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side before roasting.
Consider adding root vegetables like carrots, potatoes, and parsnips to the roasting pan during the last hour of cooking for a complete meal.
Leftover roast pork makes excellent sandwiches or can be diced and added to salads or stews.

olives.title: Marinated Olives for Saturnalia
olives.intro: Olives were a staple in ancient Roman diets, enjoyed by all social classes. During Saturnalia, the festive winter solstice celebration, tables would have been laden with simple yet delicious fare, and marinated olives would have been a welcome savory bite, perfect for sharing among friends and family as they feasted and exchanged gifts.
ingredients: 2 cups (300g) mixed olives (e.g., Kalamata, Castelvetrano, or a mix of black and green)
2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced or minced
1 sprig fresh rosemary, leaves stripped and roughly chopped
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
steps: Drain the olives from their brine and rinse them gently under cold water. Pat them dry with a clean kitchen towel.

In a medium bowl, combine the drained olives with the extra virgin olive oil, sliced or minced garlic, chopped fresh rosemary, fresh thyme leaves, dried oregano, lemon zest, and red pepper flakes (if using).
Toss everything together thoroughly to ensure the olives are well coated with the oil and seasonings.
Season with a pinch of salt and freshly ground black pepper, adjusting to your taste. Remember that olives are already salty.
Cover the bowl and let the olives marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld.
Before serving, bring the olives to room temperature for about 30 minutes to enhance their flavor. Serve them in a small bowl with toothpicks or alongside other appetizers.
tips: For an extra layer of flavor, gently warm the olive oil with the garlic and herbs for a few minutes before adding to the olives, then let it cool before combining.
Experiment with different varieties of olives; a mix of briny, buttery, and firm olives adds textural and flavor complexity.
These marinated olives can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week.

pine-nuts.title: Honey-Glazed Pine Nuts for Saturnalia
pine-nuts.intro: Saturnalia, the ancient Roman festival of feasting and merriment, was a time for rich foods and sweet treats. Pine nuts, a staple in Roman cuisine, were often combined with honey to create delightful confections. These Honey-Glazed Pine Nuts offer a simple yet elegant snack, perfect for sharing during your own festive celebrations.
steps: Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Spread the pine nuts in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Toast the pine nuts in the preheated oven for 7-10 minutes, stirring once or twice, until lightly golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
In a small saucepan, combine the honey, water, and sea salt. Heat over low heat, stirring until the honey is thinned and warm.
Remove the toasted pine nuts from the oven and immediately transfer them to a medium bowl. Pour the warm honey mixture over the pine nuts.
Stir gently with a spoon or spatula until all the pine nuts are evenly coated with the honey glaze.
Spread the glazed pine nuts back onto the baking sheet, or onto a piece of parchment paper, in a single layer to cool completely. They will become crispier as they cool.
Once cooled, break apart any clusters and serve.
tips: For an extra festive touch, add a tiny pinch of ground cinnamon or a sprinkle of orange zest to the honey mixture.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to one week.
These make a wonderful edible gift or a delightful topping for yogurt or ice cream.

mulsum-sweet-wine.title: Mulsum Sweet Wine
mulsum-sweet-wine.intro: Mulsum is a traditional Roman honeyed wine, a beloved beverage often enjoyed at feasts and celebrations, including the winter festival of Saturnalia. This simple yet elegant drink combines wine with honey, sometimes infused with spices, offering a taste of ancient Roman conviviality perfect for your holiday table.
ingredients: 1 (750 ml) bottle dry red wine (such as Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon)
1/4 to 1/2 cup (60-120 ml) honey, to taste
steps: Pour the bottle of dry red wine into a non-reactive pitcher or jar.
Add 1/4 cup (60 ml) of honey to the wine. Stir well until the honey is completely dissolved.
Taste the wine and add more honey, a tablespoon at a time, if you prefer a sweeter mulsum, stirring after each addition until dissolved.
Add the whole black peppercorns, bay leaf, and saffron threads (if using) to the wine mixture.
Stir gently to combine the spices.
Cover the pitcher or jar and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to meld.
Before serving, strain the mulsum through a fine-mesh sieve to remove the peppercorns, bay leaf, and saffron threads.
Serve chilled in small wine glasses or goblets.
tips: For a warmer, spicier note, you can gently heat the wine and honey together until the honey dissolves, then add spices and let it cool before chilling.
Experiment with other spices like a small piece of fresh ginger, a cinnamon stick, or a few cloves for different flavor profiles.
While traditionally made with red wine, a dry white wine can also be used for a lighter version of mulsum.

spiced-nuts.title: Festive Spiced Nuts
spiced-nuts.intro: These aromatic, crunchy spiced nuts are a perfect treat for the Fourth Sunday of Advent, offering warmth and comfort as Christmas approaches. They make a wonderful snack for holiday gatherings, a thoughtful homemade gift, or a cozy accompaniment to an evening of carols and reflection.
ingredients: 4 cups (450 g) mixed nuts (such as pecans, walnuts, almonds, cashews)
2 tablespoons (25 g) light brown sugar, packed
1/4 teaspoon (0.5 g) cayenne pepper (optional, for a subtle kick)
steps: Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
In a large bowl, whisk together the egg white and water until frothy.
Add the mixed nuts to the egg white mixture and toss well to ensure all nuts are evenly coated.
In a small bowl, combine the granulated sugar, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves, allspice, salt, and cayenne pepper (if using). Stir until thoroughly mixed.
Sprinkle the spice mixture over the egg white-coated nuts. Toss vigorously until all the nuts are completely and evenly coated with the spice mixture.
Spread the seasoned nuts in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring the nuts every 10-15 minutes to ensure even roasting and prevent burning. The nuts should be fragrant and feel dry to the touch.
Remove the baking sheet from the oven and let the nuts cool completely on the baking sheet. They will become crispier as they cool.
Once cooled, break apart any clusters and store the spiced nuts in an airtight container at room temperature.
tips: For a different flavor profile, try adding a pinch of cardamom or a teaspoon of orange zest to the spice mixture.
Ensure the nuts are completely cool before storing; otherwise, condensation can make them soft.
These nuts can be stored in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks, making them perfect for preparing ahead of holiday festivities.

honey-cakes.title: Saturnalia Honey Cakes
honey-cakes.intro: During Saturnalia, the ancient Roman festival of feasting and revelry, simple yet delicious treats were enjoyed by all. These Honey Cakes, reminiscent of ancient Roman confections, offer a taste of that festive spirit, symbolizing abundance and sweetness during the darkest days of winter. They are a perfect, easy-to-make addition to any Saturnalia celebration.
ingredients: 1/2 cup (120 ml) honey, plus extra for drizzling
1 tablespoon poppy seeds or sesame seeds (optional, for garnish)
steps: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour and salt.
In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the olive oil, honey, eggs, and milk (or water) until well combined.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix with a spoon or spatula until just combined. Be careful not to overmix; the dough will be thick.
Drop spoonfuls (about 1 1/2 tablespoons each) of the dough onto the prepared baking sheet, leaving approximately 2 inches (5 cm) between them as they will not spread significantly.
If desired, sprinkle the tops of the cakes with poppy seeds or sesame seeds.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the cakes are golden brown and feel firm to the touch.
Remove the baking sheet from the oven and let the cakes cool on the sheet for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally drizzled with additional honey for extra sweetness.
tips: For a more authentic ancient Roman flavor, use a robust extra virgin olive oil.
These cakes are dense and moist, similar in texture to a scone or a thick cookie, rather than a light, fluffy cake.
Store any leftover honey cakes in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days to maintain their freshness.

mince-pies.title: Traditional Mince Pies
mince-pies.intro: Mince Pies are a quintessential British Christmas treat, traditionally enjoyed throughout the Advent season and especially on Christmas Day. These delightful small pies, filled with a rich, spiced fruit mixture, are a symbol of festive cheer and a delicious way to count down to the holiday, perfect for the Fourth Sunday of Advent.
ingredients: 225 grams (1 3/4 cups) all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
110 grams (1/2 cup) cold unsalted butter, cubed
Approximately 400 grams (14 ounces) good quality jarred mincemeat
steps: In a large bowl, rub the cold butter into the flour with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Alternatively, pulse in a food processor.
Stir in the caster sugar.
Add the egg yolk and 2 tablespoons of ice cold water. Mix with a knife or your hands until the dough just comes together. If it's too dry, add the remaining tablespoon of water, a little at a time.
Gently bring the dough together into a ball, flatten slightly into a disc, wrap in plastic wrap, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Lightly grease a 12-hole muffin tin.
On a lightly floured surface, roll out about two-thirds of the chilled pastry to a thickness of about 3mm (1/8 inch).
Using a 7.5 cm (3-inch) round cutter, cut out 12 circles for the pie bases. Carefully press each circle into the prepared muffin tin holes.
Spoon about 1-2 tablespoons of mincemeat into each pastry case, filling them almost to the top.
