Do not overcrowd the baking sheet; potatoes need space to roast and crisp up. If they are too close, they will steam.
Experiment with other herbs like sage or a pinch of garlic powder for a different flavor profile.

baby-corn-gratin.title: Baby Corn Gratin
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
baby-corn-gratin.intro: Baby Corn Gratin is a comforting and creamy dish, perfect for a reflective family meal. On the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas, this warm gratin offers a sense of solace and care, honoring the memory of the innocent while providing a nourishing dish suitable for all ages at the banquet table.
ingredients: 2 (15 ounce / 425g) cans baby corn, drained and rinsed
1.5 cups (170g) shredded Gruyère or sharp cheddar cheese, divided
steps: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking dish.
If using canned baby corn, ensure it is well-drained and patted dry. If using frozen, thaw and pat dry.
In a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter. Add the flour and whisk constantly for 1-2 minutes to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk, a little at a time, ensuring no lumps form. Continue whisking until the sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from the heat. Stir in 1 cup (113g) of the shredded cheese, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until the cheese is melted and fully incorporated.
Add the drained baby corn to the cheese sauce and stir gently to coat evenly.
Pour the baby corn mixture into the prepared baking dish, spreading it into an even layer.
In a small bowl, combine the remaining 1/2 cup (57g) shredded cheese with the panko breadcrumbs. Sprinkle this mixture evenly over the top of the gratin.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the gratin is bubbly around the edges and the topping is golden brown and crisp.
Let the gratin rest for 5-10 minutes before serving to allow it to set slightly.
tips: For an extra layer of flavor, sauté a finely minced shallot or a clove of garlic in the butter before adding the flour for the roux.
This gratin can be assembled ahead of time. Cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours, then bake as directed, adding an extra 5-10 minutes to the cook time if baking from cold.
Consider adding a pinch of cayenne pepper or a dash of hot sauce to the cheese sauce for a subtle kick that complements the sweetness of the baby corn.

herb-roasted-cornish-hens.title: Herb-Roasted Cornish Hens
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
herb-roasted-cornish-hens.intro: A festive and elegant dish often served during the Christmas season, these individual herb-roasted Cornish hens make a beautiful centerpiece for a Childermas banquet. Their tender meat and aromatic herbs offer a comforting and celebratory meal, honoring the spirit of the season while acknowledging the solemnity of the Feast of the Holy Innocents on December 28th.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Pat Cornish hens dry thoroughly with paper towels, inside and out.
In a small bowl, combine softened butter, olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, dried sage, salt, and pepper. Mix well to form an herb butter.
Carefully loosen the skin over the breast and thigh meat of each hen with your fingers, creating a pocket.
Divide the herb butter mixture and spread it evenly under the skin of each hen, ensuring it covers the breast and thigh meat. Rub any remaining butter mixture over the outside skin.
Place a lemon half and an onion quarter (if using) inside the cavity of each hen. Tie the legs together with kitchen twine if desired, to help them cook evenly.
Place the hens breast-side up in a large roasting pan. Pour chicken broth into the bottom of the pan.
Roast for 50-60 minutes, or until a meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh (without touching bone) reads 165°F (74°C) and the skin is golden brown and crispy.
Remove from oven, tent loosely with foil, and let rest for 10 minutes before serving.
tips: For extra crispy skin, ensure the hens are very dry before applying the herb butter.
Basting the hens with pan juices every 20 minutes can help keep them moist and flavorful.
Serve with roasted root vegetables or wild rice for a complete and elegant holiday meal.

slow-smoked-baby-back-ribs.title: Slow-Smoked Baby Back Ribs
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
slow-smoked-baby-back-ribs.intro: While the Feast of the Holy Innocents on December 28th is a day of solemn remembrance, historical traditions often included banquets to gather families and offer comfort during the winter season. These slow-smoked baby back ribs, tender and flavorful, provide a hearty centerpiece for such a Childermas banquet, offering warmth and sustenance amidst reflection and familial gathering.
ingredients: 2 racks (about 4-5 lbs / 1.8-2.3 kg total) baby back pork ribs
Wood chips or chunks (hickory or apple wood recommended)
steps: Prepare the ribs: Remove the thin membrane from the bone-side of each rack of ribs. To do this, slide a knife under the membrane at one end, lift it, then grasp it with a paper towel and pull it off. Pat the ribs dry with paper towels.

Apply the dry rub: In a small bowl, combine all dry rub ingredients. Generously coat both sides of each rib rack with the rub, pressing it gently into the meat. Wrap the ribs tightly in plastic wrap or place them in a large sealed bag. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or preferably 4 hours up to overnight, to allow the flavors to meld.

Prepare the smoker: Preheat your smoker to a consistent temperature of 225°F (107°C). Add your chosen wood chips or chunks according to your smoker's instructions, ensuring a steady stream of thin, blue smoke.

First smoke phase: Place the seasoned ribs directly on the smoker grates, bone-side down. Smoke for 2.5 to 3 hours, maintaining the smoker temperature. During this phase, you can spritz the ribs every hour with the apple cider vinegar and apple juice mixture if desired, to keep them moist.

Wrap the ribs (the 'Texas Crutch'): Carefully remove the ribs from the smoker. Place each rack onto a large sheet of heavy-duty aluminum foil. If using the mop/spritz, lightly spray or brush the ribs one last time. Wrap each rack tightly in the foil, creating a sealed packet.

Second smoke phase: Return the foil-wrapped ribs to the smoker. Continue to cook for another 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the ribs are very tender. They are done when the meat has pulled back from the ends of the bones and a toothpick can be easily inserted between the bones with little resistance.

Finish the ribs (optional): If you desire a sticky glaze, carefully unwrap the ribs and brush them with your favorite BBQ sauce. Return the unwrapped ribs to the smoker for an additional 15-30 minutes to allow the sauce to set and caramelize.
Rest and serve: Remove the ribs from the smoker. Let them rest, loosely tented with foil, for 10-15 minutes before slicing between the bones and serving hot.
tips: For extra flavor and to help the rub adhere, spread a thin layer of yellow mustard on the ribs before applying the dry rub; it will cook off and not impart a mustard flavor.
The 'bend test' is a reliable indicator of doneness: pick up one end of a rack with tongs; if it bends significantly in the middle and the meat starts to crack, it's ready.
Serve these hearty ribs with classic winter sides like roasted root vegetables, creamy mashed potatoes, or a vibrant collard green slaw to complete your Childermas feast.

whipped-honey-butter.title: Whipped Honey Butter
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
whipped-honey-butter.intro: Whipped Honey Butter offers a touch of comforting sweetness to any festive table, making it a particularly fitting accompaniment for the Childermas Banquet. This simple yet elegant spread, often served with warm bread or rolls, provides a gentle, nourishing element to a meal that commemorates the innocence of children. Its golden hue and delicate flavor evoke warmth and simple pleasures, offering a moment of solace and joy during this reflective observance.
ingredients: 1 cup (226g) unsalted butter, softened to room temperature
1/4 cup (60mL) honey, or more to taste
1/4 teaspoon fine sea salt (optional, but recommended)
steps: Ensure the butter is thoroughly softened to room temperature; this is crucial for a smooth, airy texture.
In a medium mixing bowl, combine the softened butter, honey, and optional salt.
Using an electric mixer (handheld or stand mixer with a whisk attachment), begin mixing on low speed until the ingredients are just combined.
Increase the speed to medium-high and whip for 3-5 minutes, or until the butter is light, fluffy, and noticeably paler in color. Scrape down the sides of the bowl as needed.
Taste and adjust sweetness if desired by adding a little more honey, then whip briefly to incorporate.
Transfer the whipped honey butter to a serving dish and serve immediately, or cover and refrigerate until ready to use.
tips: If refrigerating, allow the butter to sit at room temperature for 15-20 minutes before serving to soften slightly for easier spreading.
For a hint of spice, add 1/4 teaspoon of ground cinnamon or a tiny pinch of freshly grated nutmeg during whipping.
This butter is wonderful on warm dinner rolls, cornbread, toast, pancakes, or even sweet potatoes.

warm-milk-punch.title: Warm Milk Punch
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
warm-milk-punch.intro: Warm Milk Punch is a comforting and rich beverage, perfect for the reflective atmosphere of the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas. Historically, this day on December 28th commemorated a somber event, yet feasts and gatherings would still occur, where a warm, nourishing drink like this would offer solace and warmth during the winter season.
ingredients: 1/2 cup (120 ml) heavy cream (optional, for richer punch)
1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar, or to taste
1 cup (240 ml) brandy or dark rum (or a mix)
1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg, plus more for garnish
steps: Combine the whole milk, heavy cream (if using), and granulated sugar in a medium saucepan.
Heat the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the sugar is completely dissolved and the liquid is hot but not boiling. Do not allow it to come to a boil.
Remove the saucepan from the heat.
Stir in the brandy or dark rum, vanilla extract, and the 1/4 teaspoon of ground nutmeg (and cinnamon, if using).
Taste the punch and adjust the sweetness or spice level as desired.
Ladle the warm milk punch into heatproof mugs or glasses.
Garnish each serving with a fresh grating of nutmeg before serving.
tips: For a non-alcoholic version suitable for all ages, simply omit the brandy/rum and consider adding a splash of almond extract for extra depth of flavor.
To keep the punch warm for a larger gathering, transfer it to a slow cooker set to its 'warm' setting after preparation.
Experiment with different spirits like bourbon or a spiced rum to discover varied flavor profiles for your milk punch.

babycham.title: Babycham Childermas Sparkle
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
babycham.intro: Babycham, a sparkling perry (pear cider), was a popular celebratory drink, known for its light, sweet effervescence and iconic fawn logo. For the Feast of the Holy Innocents, or Childermas Banquet, it offers a gentle, festive toast, perhaps symbolizing innocence with its light character, or simply providing a cheerful sparkle to the remembrance and feasting of the day. It's a delightful, ready-to-serve beverage perfect for raising a glass in a lighter, celebratory spirit.
ingredients: Optional: 6-12 fresh raspberries or maraschino cherries for garnish
Optional: 1 lemon, thinly sliced or twisted, for garnish
steps: Ensure your bottle of Babycham is thoroughly chilled. Ideally, refrigerate for at least 4 hours (or 240 minutes), or chill in an ice bucket for 30 minutes.
Gather your serving glasses, preferably champagne flutes or coupe glasses, and ensure they are clean and dry.
Carefully open the bottle, pointing it away from yourself and others. Gently twist the cork while holding the bottle firmly to release it slowly and safely.
Pour the Babycham slowly into each glass, tilting the glass slightly to preserve the bubbles, filling about two-thirds full.
If desired, garnish each glass with a few fresh raspberries, a maraschino cherry, or a delicate lemon twist on the rim.
Serve immediately and enjoy the festive sparkle.
tips: Always serve Babycham well-chilled (around 40-45°F or 4-7°C) for the best taste and effervescence.
For an extra touch of elegance, chill your serving glasses in the refrigerator for 15-20 minutes before pouring.
Babycham pairs wonderfully with light appetizers, fruit tarts, or simply as a standalone celebratory drink to lighten the mood of the banquet.

baby-cheesecakes.title: Baby Cheesecakes
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
baby-cheesecakes.intro: These delightful individual cheesecakes offer a sweet and comforting note to the Childermas Banquet, a gathering often held after the solemn observance of the Feast of the Holy Innocents. Their small size and delicate flavor are a gentle nod to the innocence remembered on this day, providing a moment of shared warmth and reflection among family and friends.
ingredients: Fresh berries or fruit compote, for serving (optional)
steps: Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C). Line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, combine the graham cracker crumbs and 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar. Pour in the melted butter and mix until well combined and the crumbs are moistened.
Divide the crumb mixture evenly among the 12 muffin cups, pressing it firmly into the bottom of each liner to form the crust.
In a large bowl, using an electric mixer, beat the softened cream cheese until smooth and creamy, about 2 minutes.
Gradually add the 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar to the cream cheese, beating until just combined and smooth.
Beat in the egg, vanilla extract, and salt until just incorporated. Do not overmix.
Spoon the cream cheese filling evenly over the crusts in the muffin tin, filling each cup about two-thirds full.
Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until the edges are set and the centers are just slightly jiggly.
Remove from the oven and let cool completely in the muffin tin on a wire rack.
Once cooled, transfer the cheesecakes to the refrigerator and chill for at least 2 hours, or preferably overnight, before serving.
Serve chilled, optionally topped with fresh berries or a small dollop of fruit compote.
tips: Ensure all cold ingredients, especially the cream cheese and egg, are at room temperature for a smooth, lump-free filling.
Do not overmix the cream cheese filling once the egg is added; overmixing can introduce too much air, causing the cheesecakes to crack.
These mini cheesecakes can be made a day in advance and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

pillowy-milk-rolls.title: Pillowy Milk Rolls
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
pillowy-milk-rolls.intro: These tender, slightly sweet milk rolls are a comforting addition to any meal, especially fitting for the Feast of the Holy Innocents, also known as Childermas. Their soft texture and gentle flavor symbolize the innocence and purity of children, offering a warm, nourishing presence at a banquet that commemorates the young lives lost. They are a simple yet profound way to provide comfort and sustenance during this reflective holiday.
ingredients: 1/4 cup (56 g) unsalted butter, plus 2 tablespoons (28 g) melted for brushing
2 1/4 teaspoons (7 g) active dry yeast (1 packet)
3 1/2 to 4 cups (420-480 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
steps: In a small saucepan, gently heat the milk, 1/4 cup (56 g) butter, sugar, and salt over medium-low heat until the butter is melted and the mixture is warm (about 110°F / 43°C). Do not boil.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Let stand for 5-10 minutes until the yeast is foamy.
Pour the warm milk mixture into the yeast mixture. Gradually add 3 cups (360 g) of the flour, mixing with a wooden spoon until just combined.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 5-8 minutes, adding more flour (up to 1/2 cup / 60 g) as needed, until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky.

Lightly grease a clean bowl. Place the dough in the bowl, turning once to coat. Cover with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

Gently punch down the dough. Divide it into 12-15 equal pieces. Shape each piece into a smooth ball and arrange them in a greased 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking dish, leaving a little space between them.
Cover the rolls loosely with plastic wrap or a clean towel and let them rise again in a warm place for 30-45 minutes, or until noticeably puffy.
Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
Bake the rolls for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown on top and cooked through.
As soon as the rolls come out of the oven, brush them generously with the 2 tablespoons (28 g) of melted butter.
Serve warm and enjoy.
tips: For extra richness, you can add one large egg to the milk mixture before combining with the yeast.
If your kitchen is cool, you can proof the dough in a slightly warmed (turned off) oven with the door ajar.
These rolls are best served fresh but can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in the microwave or oven.

braised-baby-onions.title: Braised Baby Onions
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
braised-baby-onions.intro: The Feast of the Holy Innocents, often observed with solemn reflection, also traditionally included special meals. These Braised Baby Onions, tender and subtly sweet, offer a comforting and symbolic side dish for a Childermas banquet. Their small size can evoke the innocence commemorated on this day, providing a gentle counterpoint to richer holiday fare.
ingredients: 1.5 pounds (680g) baby onions (such as pearl onions, cipollini, or small shallots), peeled
1/2 cup (120ml) dry white wine or dry sherry (optional)
1/4 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
steps: If using pearl onions, blanch them in boiling water for 1-2 minutes, then plunge into ice water. Trim the root end and easily slip off the skins. For cipollini or small shallots, simply peel.
In a large skillet or Dutch oven, melt the butter with the olive oil over medium heat. Add the peeled baby onions and sauté for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned on all sides.
Add the minced garlic, thyme sprig, and bay leaf to the skillet. Cook for another minute until fragrant.
Pour in the white wine (if using) and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let it reduce by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the broth, sugar, salt, and pepper. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and braise for 20-30 minutes, or until the onions are very tender when pierced with a knife.
Remove the lid and increase the heat to medium-high. Cook, stirring occasionally, for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the liquid to reduce and thicken into a glaze that coats the onions.
Remove the thyme sprig and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. Serve warm, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.
tips: For a richer, slightly tangy flavor, add a splash of balsamic vinegar during the last few minutes of cooking.
These onions can be prepared a day ahead and gently reheated on the stovetop with a little extra broth or water.
Ensure you use vegetable broth for a vegetarian or vegan version of this dish.

tableside-baby-bananas-foster.title: Tableside Baby Bananas Foster
events: Feast of the Holy Innocents (Childermas Banquet)
tableside-baby-bananas-foster.intro: Tableside Baby Bananas Foster is a dramatic and delightful dessert, perfect for a special occasion like the Childermas Banquet. Its warm, caramelized bananas and fiery presentation bring a sense of wonder and joy, making it a fitting sweet treat to celebrate the innocence and spirit of children during this reflective feast.
ingredients: 4-6 ripe baby bananas, peeled and halved lengthwise
2 tablespoons banana liqueur (optional, but enhances flavor)
1/4 cup (60ml) dark rum (such as Myers's or Bacardi Black)
Vanilla bean ice cream, for serving
steps: Prepare your serving dishes with scoops of vanilla ice cream and have them ready nearby.
In a large, heavy-bottomed skillet or chafing dish set over medium heat (ideally on a portable burner for tableside preparation), melt the butter.
Add the brown sugar and cinnamon to the melted butter. Stir continuously until the sugar is fully dissolved and the mixture forms a smooth, bubbling caramel sauce.
Gently place the halved baby bananas into the caramel sauce, cut-side down. Cook for about 1-2 minutes per side, carefully turning them once, until they are softened and coated in the sauce.
If using, pour in the banana liqueur and let it warm for about 30 seconds.

Remove the skillet briefly from the heat or turn the heat to low. Carefully pour the dark rum into the skillet. Return the skillet to the heat (if removed) or gently tilt the pan towards the flame to ignite the rum. Alternatively, use a long match or lighter to ignite the rum.
Allow the flames to subside naturally, shaking the pan gently. This process burns off the alcohol, leaving behind a rich, caramelized flavor. Do not lean over the pan while it is flaming.
Once the flames have died down, immediately spoon the warm bananas and generous amounts of the caramel sauce over the prepared vanilla ice cream.
Serve immediately and enjoy the warm, sweet, and slightly boozy dessert.
tips: For safety, ensure no flammable items are near the skillet when flambéing. Have a lid handy to smother flames if needed.
If baby bananas are unavailable, use 2-3 regular ripe but firm bananas, sliced lengthwise or into thick rounds.
A pinch of nutmeg can be added with the cinnamon for an extra layer of spice.

pomegranate-and-rosewater-cordial.title: Pomegranate and Rosewater Cordial
pomegranate-and-rosewater-cordial.intro: Pomegranate and Rosewater Cordial is a delightful and refreshing beverage, perfect for celebrating Yalda Night, the winter solstice. Pomegranates, symbols of life and rebirth, are central to this ancient Persian festival, and their tart sweetness is beautifully complemented by the fragrant, delicate notes of rosewater, creating a festive and traditional drink.
pomegranate-and-rosewater-cordial.yield: Makes about 2 cups (480 ml) of cordial concentrate, enough for 8-10 servings when diluted
ingredients: 4 large pomegranates (yielding about 2 cups / 480 ml juice)
1/2 cup (120 ml) water (optional, for desired consistency)
steps: Carefully cut the pomegranates and extract the seeds. Juice the seeds using a juicer, blender (then strain), or by hand, to yield about 2 cups (480 ml) of fresh pomegranate juice. Strain the juice through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any pulp or seeds.
In a medium saucepan, combine the strained pomegranate juice, granulated sugar, and water (if using).

Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the sugar completely dissolves. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and continue to cook for 10-12 minutes, or until the syrup slightly thickens. Do not boil vigorously.
Remove the saucepan from the heat. Stir in the rosewater and fresh lemon juice.
Allow the cordial to cool completely to room temperature.
Once cooled, pour the cordial into a clean, airtight bottle or jar.
To serve, dilute 1 part cordial with 3-4 parts cold water or sparkling water, adjusting to your taste. Garnish with fresh pomegranate seeds or a mint sprig.
tips: For a richer flavor, you can reduce the cordial for a few extra minutes, but be careful not to caramelize the sugar.
Store the cordial in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 weeks.
This cordial can also be used as a mixer for cocktails, drizzled over desserts, or added to iced tea for a floral, fruity twist.

fresh-herb-platter-with-feta-and-walnuts.title: Fresh Herb Platter with Feta and Walnuts
fresh-herb-platter-with-feta-and-walnuts.dish: Fresh Herb Platter with Feta and Walnuts
fresh-herb-platter-with-feta-and-walnuts.intro: This vibrant Fresh Herb Platter, known as Sabzi Khordan, is a quintessential element of Yalda Night, the ancient Persian celebration of the winter solstice. Symbolizing freshness, vitality, and the bounty of nature, it's a refreshing counterpoint to richer dishes and a beautiful centerpiece for the longest night of the year.
ingredients: 1 bunch (about 1 cup or 25 g) fresh mint, leaves picked
1 bunch (about 1 cup or 25 g) fresh basil, leaves picked
1/2 bunch (about 1/2 cup or 12 g) fresh tarragon, leaves picked (optional)
1/2 bunch (about 1/2 cup or 12 g) fresh cilantro, leaves picked
1/2 bunch (about 1/2 cup or 12 g) fresh parsley, leaves picked
4-6 green onions (scallions), trimmed and cut into 2-inch (5 cm) pieces
1/2 pound (225 g) feta cheese, crumbled or cut into small cubes
1 cup (120 g) walnuts, halves or pieces
4-6 radishes, trimmed and thinly sliced or left whole
Lavash or Sangak bread, for serving
steps: Thoroughly wash all fresh herbs under cold running water. Gently pat them dry with paper towels or use a salad spinner to remove excess moisture.
Arrange the washed and dried herbs artfully on a large serving platter or board.
Scatter the crumbled or cubed feta cheese over the herbs.
Distribute the walnuts evenly across the platter.
Arrange the sliced radishes and optional cucumber slices among the herbs, cheese, and walnuts.
Serve immediately with fresh lavash or sangak bread on the side, allowing guests to tear off pieces of bread and create small bites with the herbs, cheese, and walnuts.
tips: For the best flavor and presentation, use a variety of fresh, vibrant herbs. Don't be afraid to mix and match based on availability.
Ensure all herbs are completely dry after washing to prevent them from wilting quickly and to maintain their crispness.
Offer a small bowl of sea salt or a sprinkle of dried mint on the side for those who enjoy an extra touch of flavor.

marinated-olives-with-pomegranate-and-wa.title: Marinated Olives with Pomegranate and Walnuts
marinated-olives-with-pomegranate-and-wa.dish: Marinated Olives with Pomegranate and Walnuts
marinated-olives-with-pomegranate-and-wa.intro: This vibrant dish is a delightful addition to the Yalda Night (Shab-e Yalda) spread, celebrating the winter solstice and the longest night of the year. Pomegranates are a quintessential symbol of Yalda, representing life and rebirth, and when combined with briny olives and crunchy walnuts, they create a festive and flavorful appetizer that perfectly complements the traditional fruits and nuts of the occasion.
ingredients: 2 cups (about 300g) mixed pitted olives, such as Kalamata and Castelvetrano
1/2 cup (75g) pomegranate arils (from about 1/2 a large pomegranate)
Pinch of sea salt (optional, depending on olive saltiness)
steps: Rinse the pitted olives gently under cold water and pat them dry with a paper towel. Place them in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
Add the pomegranate arils and chopped walnuts to the bowl with the olives.
In a small separate bowl, whisk together the pomegranate juice, olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, chopped mint, chopped parsley, and black pepper.
Pour the dressing over the olive mixture. Gently toss all ingredients together until everything is well coated.
Taste and add a pinch of sea salt if needed, keeping in mind that olives are already quite salty.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld. For best results, marinate for 2-4 hours.
Before serving, give the mixture another gentle stir and serve chilled or at room temperature.
tips: For an extra layer of flavor, lightly toast the walnuts in a dry skillet for a few minutes until fragrant before chopping.
A touch of orange zest can be added to the marinade for a brighter, citrusy note.
This dish can be prepared a day in advance; the flavors will deepen beautifully overnight in the refrigerator.

shirazi-salad.title: Shirazi Salad
shirazi-salad.intro: Shirazi Salad is a classic Persian salad, known for its refreshing and vibrant flavors. Made with finely diced cucumbers, tomatoes, and red onion, dressed simply with fresh lime juice and olive oil, it's a staple at many Persian meals. For Yalda Night, the winter solstice celebration, its fresh ingredients symbolize the bounty of nature and offer a light, palate-cleansing contrast to richer dishes, making it a perfect accompaniment to the festive spread.
ingredients: 3 Persian cucumbers (or 1 large English cucumber), finely diced (approx. 300g)
3 ripe Roma tomatoes, finely diced (or 2 medium regular tomatoes), seeds removed (approx. 300g)
3 tablespoons fresh lime juice (approx. 45ml), from 1-2 limes
1/4 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
steps: Wash and finely dice the cucumbers, tomatoes, and red onion into small, uniform pieces (about 1/4 inch or 0.6 cm cubes). For tomatoes, you may remove the seeds if desired for a less watery salad.
Place the diced vegetables into a medium-sized mixing bowl.
Add the finely chopped fresh mint to the bowl with the vegetables.
In a small separate bowl, whisk together the fresh lime juice, extra virgin olive oil, salt, and black pepper to create the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the diced vegetables and mint.
Gently toss all the ingredients together until well combined and evenly coated with the dressing.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, adding more salt, pepper, or lime juice to your preference.
Serve immediately, or chill in the refrigerator for at least 15-30 minutes before serving for enhanced flavor.
tips: For an extra layer of flavor, add 1/2 teaspoon of dried mint or a pinch of sumac to the dressing.
Ensure all vegetables are diced very finely and uniformly; this is key to the salad's traditional texture and flavor distribution.
Shirazi Salad is best served fresh, but it can be prepared a few hours in advance and kept chilled. Toss again before serving.

beet-yogurt-dip-with-pistachio.title: Beet Yogurt Dip with Pistachio
beet-yogurt-dip-with-pistachio.intro: This vibrant Beet Yogurt Dip, known as Borani Laboo in Persian cuisine, is a refreshing and visually stunning addition to any Yalda Night spread. Yalda Night, or Shab-e Yalda, celebrates the winter solstice, the longest night of the year, and is traditionally marked by gathering with loved ones, reading poetry, and enjoying seasonal fruits like pomegranates and watermelon, as well as colorful dishes like this one. The deep red of the beets symbolizes the dawn and the warmth of the sun, making it a perfect dish to welcome the longer days ahead.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon (15ml) extra virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
1/4 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
1/4 cup (30g) shelled pistachios, roughly chopped, for garnish
2 tablespoons fresh mint or dill, chopped, for garnish (optional)
steps: Wash the beets thoroughly. Place them in a medium pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 30-45 minutes, or until fork-tender. Alternatively, roast beets wrapped in foil at 400°F (200°C) for 45-60 minutes until tender.
Once cooked, drain the beets and let them cool slightly. When cool enough to handle, peel the skin off (it should slip off easily).
Roughly chop the cooked and peeled beets. In a food processor, combine the chopped beets, minced garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Process until the mixture is smooth, scraping down the sides as needed. You can leave it slightly chunky if you prefer a different texture.
Transfer the beet mixture to a medium bowl. Add the Greek yogurt and gently fold it in until just combined and uniformly pink. Do not overmix.
Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, adding more salt, pepper, or lemon juice to your preference.
Cover the dip and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and for the dip to chill.

Before serving, transfer the dip to a serving bowl. Drizzle with a little extra olive oil and sprinkle generously with the chopped pistachios and fresh herbs, if using. Serve with pita bread, crackers, or fresh vegetables.
tips: For a deeper, sweeter flavor, roast the beets instead of boiling them. This caramelizes their natural sugars.
Adjust the amount of garlic to your liking; for a milder flavor, use just one clove, or for a stronger kick, add a third.
This dip can be made a day ahead and stored in the refrigerator. The flavors will deepen overnight, just give it a good stir before serving and add fresh garnishes.

yalda-night-mixed-nuts-and-dried-fruits.title: Yalda Night Ajeel (Mixed Nuts and Dried Fruits)
yalda-night-mixed-nuts-and-dried-fruits.dish: Yalda Night Mixed Nuts and Dried Fruits
yalda-night-mixed-nuts-and-dried-fruits.intro: Yalda Night, or Shab-e Yalda, marks the winter solstice and the longest night of the year, a cherished ancient Persian celebration of light overcoming darkness. Ajeel, a vibrant mix of nuts and dried fruits, is a cornerstone of the Yalda spread, symbolizing abundance, health, and the bounty of the harvest, enjoyed by families gathered together to read poetry and share stories.
ingredients: 1 cup (120 g) almonds, raw or lightly roasted
1/2 cup (60 g) hazelnuts, raw or lightly roasted
1/2 cup (60 g) cashews, raw or lightly roasted
1/2 cup (75 g) dried figs, quartered or halved
steps: Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C) if you wish to lightly toast the raw nuts and seeds. Skip this step if using pre-roasted nuts.
Spread raw walnuts, almonds, hazelnuts, cashews, pumpkin seeds, and sunflower seeds in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Toast in the preheated oven for 8-10 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until fragrant and lightly golden. Be careful not to burn them.
Remove from the oven and let the toasted nuts and seeds cool completely on the baking sheet.
In a large decorative bowl, combine the cooled toasted nuts and seeds with the pistachios, golden raisins, dark raisins, dried mulberries, dried figs, and dried apricots.
If desired, sprinkle with a pinch of sea salt for enhanced flavor.
Gently toss all the ingredients together until well combined.
Arrange the ajeel attractively in serving bowls, often alongside fresh pomegranates and watermelon, for your Yalda Night celebration.
tips: For the best flavor, use high-quality, fresh nuts and dried fruits. Avoid anything that smells stale or rancid.
Customize your ajeel by adding other favorites like dried cranberries, dates, or even roasted chickpeas (nokhodchi).
Store any leftover ajeel in an airtight container at room temperature for up to two weeks, or in the refrigerator for longer freshness.

walnut-pomegranate-stew-fesenjan.title: Fesenjan (Persian Walnut and Pomegranate Stew)
walnut-pomegranate-stew-fesenjan.intro: Fesenjan is a rich, savory-sweet stew, a jewel of Persian cuisine, traditionally enjoyed during special occasions like Yalda Night. Its deep, complex flavors from ground walnuts and tart pomegranate molasses symbolize the richness and warmth desired during the longest night of the year, offering comfort and celebration as families gather.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons olive oil or vegetable oil
1.5 lbs (680g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1.5-inch (4cm) pieces
3-4 cups (720-960ml) hot water or chicken broth
Pomegranate arils and fresh parsley, for garnish (optional)
steps: Spread the walnuts in a single layer on a baking sheet. Toast in a preheated oven at 350°F (175°C) for 8-10 minutes, or until fragrant and lightly golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Once cooled, transfer the toasted walnuts to a food processor and process until very finely ground into a paste-like consistency. Be careful not to over-process into butter.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add the chicken pieces to the pot and brown them on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. You don't need to cook them through, just get a nice color.
Stir in the turmeric powder, black pepper, and salt with the chicken and onions. Cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add the finely ground walnuts to the pot. Stir well to combine with the chicken and onions, and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently, to lightly toast the walnuts further.
Pour in the pomegranate molasses and 3 cups (720ml) of hot water or broth. Stir everything together. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.

Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the stew simmer for at least 2 hours, or up to 3 hours, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. The longer it simmers, the richer the flavor and the more oil will rise from the walnuts.

After 2 hours, check the consistency; if it's too thick, add the remaining 1 cup (240ml) of hot water or broth. Taste the stew and add sugar, one tablespoon at a time, if you prefer a slightly sweeter balance to the tartness of the pomegranate molasses.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh pomegranate arils and chopped parsley if desired, typically with Persian steamed rice (chelo).
tips: For a richer stew and to encourage the walnuts to release their oils, add 3-4 ice cubes to the stew during the last hour of simmering. The sudden temperature drop helps separate the oil.
Vegetarian option: Replace chicken with roasted butternut squash chunks, sautéed mushrooms, or pre-cooked vegetarian meatballs, adding them during the last 30-45 minutes of simmering.
The tartness of pomegranate molasses varies. Always taste and adjust the amount of sugar to achieve your preferred balance of sweet and sour.

saffron-rice-cake-with-barberries-and-ch.title: Saffron Rice Cake with Barberries and Chicken (Tahchin)
saffron-rice-cake-with-barberries-and-ch.dish: Saffron Rice Cake with Barberries and Chicken (Tahchin)
saffron-rice-cake-with-barberries-and-ch.intro: Tahchin is a beautiful and flavorful layered Persian rice dish, often served for special occasions and celebrations. For Yalda Night, the winter solstice, it graces the table as a symbol of warmth, abundance, and the vibrant colors of the season, especially with its golden crust and ruby red barberries.
ingredients: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts
1.5 cups (360 g) full-fat plain yogurt (Greek yogurt works well)
1/2 cup (120 ml) vegetable oil or ghee, plus 2 tablespoons for barberries
2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter (optional, for richness)
Salt and black pepper to taste
1/4 cup (30 g) slivered pistachios or almonds (optional, for garnish)
steps: Prepare Saffron: Grind saffron threads with a mortar and pestle. Steep in 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water or 2-3 ice cubes for at least 15 minutes to release color and flavor.

Cook Chicken: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pan over medium heat. Sauté chopped onion until translucent. Add chicken pieces, turmeric, salt, and pepper. Cook until chicken is lightly browned. Add 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until cooked through. Shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces and set aside.

Par-boil Rice: Wash rice thoroughly until water runs clear. Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add the washed rice and cook for 7-10 minutes, or until the grains are tender on the outside but still firm in the center (al dente). Drain immediately in a colander and rinse briefly with cool water to stop cooking.
Prepare Yogurt Mixture: In a large bowl, whisk together yogurt, egg yolks, 1/4 cup (60 ml) of the prepared saffron water, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and a pinch of black pepper.
Combine Rice and Yogurt: Gently fold about 3 cups (approx. 450 g) of the par-boiled rice into the yogurt mixture until well combined. This will be the bottom layer.

Assemble Tahchin: Choose a non-stick pot with a tight-fitting lid (a 10-inch/25 cm pot works well). Pour 1/2 cup (120 ml) vegetable oil into the pot and swirl to coat the bottom and sides. If using butter, add it now.
Layer 1 (Tahdig): Spread the yogurt-rice mixture evenly over the bottom of the pot, pressing down gently to form a compact layer.
Layer 2 (Chicken): Arrange the shredded chicken evenly over the yogurt-rice layer.

Layer 3 (Remaining Rice): Gently mound the remaining plain par-boiled rice over the chicken. Create a few holes in the rice with the handle of a spoon to allow steam to escape. Pour the remaining saffron water over the top of the rice.

Cook Tahchin: Cover the pot with a lid, preferably wrapped in a clean kitchen towel to absorb steam. Cook on medium-high heat for 10-15 minutes until steam builds up. Then reduce heat to low and cook for an additional 50-60 minutes, or until a golden crust (tahdig) forms at the bottom.

Prepare Barberries: While the tahchin cooks, melt 2 tablespoons oil or butter in a small pan over low heat. Add barberries and sugar. Sauté for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until plump and glossy (do not burn). Remove from heat.

Serve: Once cooked, remove the pot from heat and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. Place a large serving platter over the pot and carefully invert the tahchin onto the platter. Garnish with the prepared barberries and optional slivered pistachios or almonds. Serve warm.
tips: For an extra crispy tahdig, ensure the oil is hot before adding the first layer of rice and don't rush the initial high-heat cooking.
If you prefer a vegetarian version, omit the chicken and add sautéed mushrooms or eggplant slices instead.
The quality of saffron makes a big difference; use good quality threads for the best color and aroma.

okra-stew-khoresht-e-bamieh.title: Okra Stew (Khoresht-e Bamieh)
okra-stew-khoresht-e-bamieh.intro: Khoresht-e Bamieh, or Okra Stew, is a beloved Persian stew known for its tender okra pods and rich tomato-based sauce, often featuring succulent pieces of meat. While enjoyed year-round, its comforting warmth and hearty nature make it a wonderful addition to the Yalda Night feast, symbolizing abundance and shared sustenance during the longest night of the year.
ingredients: 1 pound (450 g) lamb or beef stew meat, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
2 cups (480 ml) beef or vegetable broth, or water
1/2 teaspoon black pepper, or to taste
1 pound (450 g) fresh or frozen okra, trimmed
2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice, or 1-2 dried limes (limoo amani), pierced
steps: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the cubed lamb or beef to the pot and brown on all sides, stirring occasionally, about 8-10 minutes. Drain any excess fat if necessary.
Stir in the minced garlic and ground turmeric, cooking for another minute until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, broth (or water), salt, and black pepper to the pot. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 1 hour, or until the meat is tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
If using fresh okra, you may wish to quickly sauté it in a separate pan with a teaspoon of oil for 5 minutes before adding to the stew to reduce sliminess. If using frozen okra, add directly.
Add the trimmed okra and fresh lemon juice (or pierced dried limes) to the stew. Gently stir to combine.
Continue to simmer, uncovered, for another 15-20 minutes, or until the okra is tender but still holds its shape. Be careful not to overcook the okra, as it can become mushy.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Remove dried limes if used before serving.
Serve Khoresht-e Bamieh hot, traditionally with fluffy Basmati rice.
tips: For a vegetarian version, omit the meat and use vegetable broth, adding chickpeas or lentils for protein during the last 30 minutes of cooking.
If using fresh okra, trimming just the very tip of the stem without cutting into the pod can help minimize sliminess.
This stew tastes even better the next day, as the flavors have more time to meld. It can be made ahead and gently reheated.

barbari-bread.title: Barbari Bread
barbari-bread.intro: Barbari bread is a beloved traditional Persian flatbread, distinguished by its elongated shape, crispy crust, and soft, airy interior. It is a staple at Yalda Night, the ancient Persian celebration of the winter solstice, where it's often served alongside feta cheese, fresh herbs, and the symbolic fruits of the longest night, like watermelon and pomegranates.
ingredients: 4 cups (480 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil, plus more for greasing
2 tablespoons (30 g) sesame seeds (white, black, or a mix)
steps: In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and 1 teaspoon of sugar. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
Add the 4 cups of flour and salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
Add the 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it is smooth and elastic. The dough should be slightly sticky.

Lightly grease a clean large bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

While the dough is rising, prepare the Roomal (glaze): In a small saucepan, whisk together the 1/4 cup flour, 1/2 cup water, 1/2 teaspoon sugar, and baking soda until smooth. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens to a thin, gravy-like consistency. Remove from heat and let it cool completely.
Once the dough has risen, gently punch it down and divide it into two equal pieces.

On a piece of parchment paper (or a lightly floured surface), gently stretch and shape each piece of dough into an elongated oval or rectangular shape, about 12-14 inches (30-35 cm) long and 5-6 inches (12-15 cm) wide. Transfer the parchment paper with the dough to a baking sheet.
Using your fingertips, gently press parallel indentations (ridges) along the length of each loaf, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) apart. Be careful not to press all the way through the dough.
Cover the shaped loaves loosely with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel and let them rise again for 20-30 minutes, or until slightly puffy.
Preheat your oven to 450°F (230°C) with a baking stone or an inverted baking sheet inside, if you have one, for at least 30 minutes.
Just before baking, generously brush the cooled Roomal glaze over the surface of each loaf, ensuring it gets into the indentations. Sprinkle evenly with sesame seeds.
Carefully transfer the parchment paper with the loaves onto the preheated baking stone or baking sheet. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and crispy.
Remove the bread from the oven and transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly before slicing and serving.
tips: For an extra crispy crust, place a shallow pan of hot water on the bottom rack of your oven during baking to create steam.
The Roomal glaze is key to Barbari's unique texture and shine; ensure it's cool before applying.
Barbari is best enjoyed warm, fresh from the oven, with a spread of feta cheese and fresh herbs like mint and basil.

pomegranate-and-watermelon.title: Pomegranate and Watermelon Platter for Yalda Night
pomegranate-and-watermelon.intro: Yalda Night, the longest night of the year, is an ancient Persian celebration of the winter solstice. Pomegranates and watermelons are iconic symbols of this festival, representing the warmth of summer, the dawn, and the cycle of life. This simple platter highlights their natural beauty and vibrant flavors, bringing good fortune and health to the gathering.
ingredients: 1/4 cup (30 g) shelled pistachios, roughly chopped (optional, for garnish)
steps: Prepare the pomegranates: Score the pomegranates around their equator, then gently pull them apart. Submerge the halves in a bowl of cold water and, while underwater, use your fingers to dislodge the seeds from the white membrane. The seeds will sink, and the membrane will float. Skim off the membrane, then drain the seeds in a colander.
Prepare the watermelon: Cut the watermelon into bite-sized cubes or elegant wedges, removing any remaining seeds if necessary.
Arrange the platter: On a large serving platter, artfully arrange the watermelon pieces.
Add pomegranate seeds: Generously sprinkle the fresh pomegranate seeds over and around the watermelon.
Garnish: If using, lightly drizzle the rosewater over the fruit. Sprinkle with chopped pistachios and scatter fresh mint leaves for a beautiful presentation.
Serve immediately: Present the vibrant platter as a centerpiece for your Yalda Night celebration.
tips: For an extra touch of sweetness, a light sprinkle of sugar or a drizzle of honey can be added, though the fruits are usually sweet enough on their own.
To make preparation easier, you can deseed the pomegranates a day in advance and store the seeds in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
Other traditional Yalda fruits like persimmons or apples can be added to the platter for more variety and color.

cranberry-relish.title: Classic Homemade Cranberry Relish
cranberry-relish.intro: Cranberry Relish is an essential, vibrant side dish for Thanksgiving Day in the United States, offering a bright, tart counterpoint to the rich flavors of turkey, stuffing, and gravy. This simple, homemade version is far superior to canned varieties, bringing a fresh burst of flavor that truly elevates the holiday meal.
ingredients: 12 ounces (340 g) fresh or frozen cranberries
1 cup (240 ml) water or orange juice
steps: Rinse the cranberries thoroughly and pick out any soft or bruised berries.
In a medium saucepan, combine the sugar, water (or orange juice), and orange zest.
Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring until the sugar is dissolved.
Add the cranberries to the boiling liquid.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer gently for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until most of the cranberries have burst and the relish has thickened.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and let the relish cool completely at room temperature.
Transfer the cooled relish to a serving bowl or airtight container.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving to allow the flavors to meld and the relish to thicken further.
tips: For an extra layer of flavor, add a pinch of ground cinnamon or a tiny piece of fresh ginger during simmering.
This relish can be made up to a week in advance and stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator, making Thanksgiving meal prep easier.
If you prefer a chunkier relish, simmer for a shorter time; for a smoother consistency, gently mash some of the berries with the back of a spoon as they cook.

cornbread-stuffing.title: Classic Cornbread Stuffing
cornbread-stuffing.intro: Cornbread Stuffing is a beloved staple on many Thanksgiving tables across the United States, offering a delightful Southern twist to the traditional holiday dressing. Its slightly sweet and crumbly texture, combined with savory herbs and vegetables, makes it a comforting and essential side dish that perfectly complements roasted turkey and gravy.
ingredients: 8 cups (about 1.5 lbs or 680g) crumbled day-old cornbread
1 tablespoon fresh sage, chopped (or 1 teaspoon dried)
1 tablespoon fresh thyme, chopped (or 1 teaspoon dried)
3-4 cups (720-960ml) chicken or vegetable broth, warm
steps: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking dish.

Spread the crumbled cornbread on a large baking sheet and toast in the preheated oven for 10-15 minutes, or until lightly golden and slightly dried out. This helps prevent a soggy stuffing. Remove from oven and set aside.
In a large skillet or Dutch oven, melt 1/2 cup (113g) of the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and celery and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add the minced garlic, fresh sage, and fresh thyme to the skillet. Cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the toasted cornbread crumbs, the sautéed onion and celery mixture, salt, and pepper. Toss gently to combine.
In a separate small bowl, whisk the eggs. Pour the beaten eggs over the cornbread mixture and mix well.

Gradually add 3 cups (720ml) of the warm broth to the cornbread mixture, stirring until just moistened. The mixture should be moist but not soupy. Add more broth, a little at a time, if it seems too dry.
Melt the remaining 1/2 cup (113g) of butter. Pour half of it into the cornbread mixture and stir gently to incorporate.
Transfer the stuffing mixture to the prepared baking dish. Drizzle the remaining melted butter over the top.
Bake for 30-40 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the stuffing is heated through and slightly crisp on top. If the top browns too quickly, you can loosely cover it with foil.
tips: For extra flavor, sauté 1/2 pound (225g) of crumbled breakfast sausage or diced mushrooms with the onions and celery.
Add 1/2 cup (60g) of chopped pecans or dried cranberries to the mixture for added texture and a touch of sweetness.
Prepare the cornbread a day or two in advance to ensure it's stale enough for the best stuffing texture.

pie.title: Classic Thanksgiving Pumpkin Pie
pie.intro: Pumpkin pie is the quintessential dessert for Thanksgiving Day in the United States, symbolizing the harvest and the bounty of the season. Its warm spices and creamy texture provide a comforting and traditional end to the holiday feast, often served with a dollop of whipped cream. This recipe delivers a perfectly spiced and smooth pumpkin pie that will be a beloved addition to your holiday table.
ingredients: 1 (9-inch / 23 cm) unbaked pie crust (store-bought or homemade)
1 (15-ounce / 425 g) can pumpkin puree (not pumpkin pie filling)
steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C).
Place the unbaked pie crust into a 9-inch (23 cm) pie plate.
In a large bowl, combine the pumpkin puree, evaporated milk, granulated sugar, salt, ground cinnamon, ground ginger, and ground cloves.
Whisk the ingredients together until they are well combined and smooth.
Add the lightly beaten eggs to the pumpkin mixture and stir until just incorporated.
Pour the pumpkin filling carefully into the unbaked pie crust.
Bake for 15 minutes at 425°F (220°C).
Reduce the oven temperature to 350°F (175°C) and continue baking for 35-45 minutes, or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean.
Remove the pie from the oven and let it cool completely on a wire rack before slicing and serving. This allows the filling to set properly.
tips: For best results, allow the pie to cool for at least 2-3 hours before serving, or even overnight, to ensure the filling is fully set.
Serve chilled or at room temperature, often topped with a generous dollop of whipped cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
If the crust edges start to brown too quickly, you can cover them loosely with aluminum foil during the last part of baking.

green-bean-casserole.title: Classic Green Bean Casserole
green-bean-casserole.intro: Green Bean Casserole is a quintessential side dish that graces nearly every Thanksgiving table across the United States. This creamy, savory bake, topped with crispy fried onions, offers a comforting contrast to the richer flavors of the holiday feast, making it a beloved and eagerly anticipated part of the annual celebration.
ingredients: 2 (14.5 ounce / 411 g) cans cut green beans, drained
1 (10.5 ounce / 298 g) can condensed cream of mushroom soup
1 (6 ounce / 170 g) can French fried onions
steps: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
In a large mixing bowl, combine the condensed cream of mushroom soup, milk, soy sauce, and black pepper. Stir until the mixture is smooth and well blended.
Add the drained green beans and 1/2 of the French fried onions to the soup mixture. Stir gently to ensure the beans are evenly coated.
Pour the entire mixture into a 1.5-quart (1.4 L) casserole dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the casserole is hot and bubbly.
Remove the casserole from the oven and sprinkle the remaining French fried onions evenly over the top.
Return the casserole to the oven and bake for an additional 5-10 minutes, or until the onions are golden brown and crispy.
Serve hot and enjoy this classic holiday side dish.
tips: For a fresher take, substitute canned green beans with 1.5 pounds (680 g) fresh green beans, trimmed and blanched, or 2 (10 ounce / 283 g) packages frozen green beans, thawed.
Add 1/2 cup (50 g) shredded sharp cheddar cheese or a sprinkle of crumbled cooked bacon to the mixture before baking for an extra layer of flavor.
Ensure your French fried onions are fresh; stale onions won't achieve the desired crispiness.

sweet-potatoes.title: Sweet Potato Casserole with Pecan Topping
sweet-potatoes.intro: Sweet Potato Casserole is a beloved staple on many American Thanksgiving tables, offering a delightful balance of sweet and savory flavors. Often served alongside turkey and other traditional dishes, its creamy texture and crunchy pecan topping make it a comforting and festive addition to the holiday feast.
ingredients: 4 lbs (1.8 kg) sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, melted, plus more for greasing
1/2 cup (120 ml) whole milk or half-and-half
1/4 cup (50 g) packed light brown sugar
1/2 cup (100 g) packed light brown sugar
steps: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking dish with butter.
Place the peeled and cubed sweet potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain the sweet potatoes thoroughly and return them to the pot. Mash them with a potato masher or an electric mixer until smooth.

Add the 1/2 cup (113 g) melted butter, milk, granulated sugar, 1/4 cup (50 g) brown sugar, eggs, vanilla extract, and salt to the mashed sweet potatoes. Mix well until everything is fully combined and smooth.
Pour the sweet potato mixture into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly.

In a medium bowl, combine the chopped pecans, 1/2 cup (100 g) brown sugar, and flour for the topping. Pour the 1/4 cup (57 g) melted butter over the mixture and stir with a fork until crumbly and well combined.
Evenly sprinkle the pecan topping over the sweet potato mixture in the baking dish.

Bake for 30 minutes, then loosely tent with foil to prevent the topping from over-browning, and continue baking for another 15-20 minutes, or until the casserole is heated through and the topping is golden brown and bubbly.
Remove from the oven and let rest for 5-10 minutes before serving.
tips: For a make-ahead option, prepare the sweet potato mixture and topping separately, then assemble and bake on Thanksgiving Day.
If you prefer a sweeter casserole, you can increase the amount of granulated sugar in the sweet potato base by 1/4 cup (50 g).

For a classic marshmallow topping variation, omit the pecan topping and instead, during the last 10-15 minutes of baking, cover the casserole with 4-5 cups (200-250 g) of mini marshmallows and bake until golden brown and puffed.

saffron-rice-pudding-sholeh-zard.title: Saffron Rice Pudding (Sholeh Zard)
saffron-rice-pudding-sholeh-zard.intro: Sholeh Zard is a fragrant and delicate Persian saffron rice pudding, often prepared for special occasions and religious holidays. It's a beloved dish for Yalda Night, the winter solstice celebration, symbolizing warmth and light during the longest night of the year, often enjoyed as a sweet ending to the festive meal.
ingredients: 1 cup (200 g) short-grain white rice (such as Basmati or Jasmine)
6 cups (1.4 liters) water, plus more if needed
1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water or milk (for saffron)
1/4 cup (30 g) slivered almonds, for garnish
1/4 cup (30 g) chopped pistachios, for garnish
steps: Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. Soak the rice in cold water for at least 1 hour, then drain.

Crush the saffron threads into a fine powder using a mortar and pestle or by pressing with the back of a spoon. Place the crushed saffron in a small bowl and add 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water or milk. Let it steep for at least 10-15 minutes to bloom and release its color and aroma.

In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, combine the drained rice and 6 cups (1.4 liters) of fresh water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until the rice is very tender and has absorbed most of the water, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Once the rice is very soft and mushy, add the granulated sugar, bloomed saffron (including the liquid), rosewater, unsalted butter, and optional ground cardamom to the pot. Stir well to combine.

Continue to cook on low heat, stirring frequently, for another 15-20 minutes, or until the pudding has thickened to a creamy consistency. It should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon but still pourable. Add a little more hot water if it becomes too thick.
Remove the pot from the heat. Pour the Sholeh Zard into individual serving bowls or a large serving dish.
Allow the pudding to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2-3 hours, or until thoroughly chilled and set.
Before serving, garnish generously with slivered almonds, chopped pistachios, and a decorative pattern of ground cinnamon.
tips: For an extra smooth texture, you can mash some of the rice against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon while cooking.
Adjust the amount of sugar to your preference; some like it sweeter, some less so.
Sholeh Zard is traditionally served cold, which allows its flavors to fully develop and its texture to firm up beautifully.

calabaza-en-tacha.title: Calabaza en Tacha (Candied Pumpkin)
events: Día de Muertos Celebration at the Fine Arts Center
Día de Muertos at the Children’s Museum of Denver
calabaza-en-tacha.intro: Calabaza en tacha is a traditional Mexican pumpkin dessert enjoyed during Día de Muertos. Pumpkin wedges simmer gently in piloncillo and cinnamon syrup until tender. The edible flesh is served with syrup; the rind helps the pieces hold their shape.
ingredients: 1 small cooking pumpkin or kabocha squash, about 3 lb (1.4 kg)
12 oz (340 g) piloncillo, chopped, or packed dark brown sugar
3 cups (720 ml) water, plus more as needed
2 wide strips orange peel, washed, with minimal white pith (optional)
steps: Wash and dry the pumpkin. On a stable cutting board, carefully halve it and scoop out the seeds and stringy pulp. Cut into thick wedges about 2–3 inches wide, leaving the rind on.
In a wide, heavy pot, combine the piloncillo, water, cinnamon, optional cloves and orange peel, and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Arrange the pumpkin wedges in the pot, rind side down where possible. Spoon syrup over the flesh. The syrup need not cover the pumpkin completely.

Cover and simmer gently for 45–75 minutes, depending on the thickness and variety of pumpkin. Baste every 15–20 minutes and add a little hot water if the syrup gets too low. Avoid stirring or boiling vigorously so the wedges stay intact.

When a fork slides easily into the flesh, carefully transfer the wedges to a serving dish. If the syrup is thin, simmer it uncovered for 10–15 minutes until lightly thickened; it will thicken further as it cools. Remove the cinnamon, cloves and orange peel.
Pour the syrup over the pumpkin. Serve warm or at room temperature, with a splash of milk or cream if desired. Scoop the soft flesh away from any tough rind.
tips: Use a cooking pumpkin or a dense winter squash, rather than a large carving pumpkin.
This version uses moderate sweetness; drizzle on more syrup to taste.
Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours and use within 3–4 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water.

torro-dagramunt.title: Torró d’Agramunt
torro-dagramunt.intro: Torró d’Agramunt is a traditional Catalan nougat from Agramunt, made with toasted hazelnuts or almonds, honey, sugar, egg white, and edible wafer. This home-style hazelnut version is a sweet for our Christmas Eve Tió festivities.
ingredients: 2 sheets edible wafer paper (oblea), sized to an 8-inch (20 cm) square pan
steps: Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Toast the hazelnuts on a tray for 10–15 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden. Rub off loose skins in a clean towel. Keep the nuts warm in the switched-off oven.
Line an 8-inch (20 cm) square pan with baking parchment, leaving an overhang. Place a sheet of edible wafer paper on the bottom. Have the second sheet and a sturdy, lightly oiled spatula ready.

Put the honey, sugar, and water in a heavy saucepan with room for bubbling. Warm gently, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Bring to a boil without stirring and cook to 300°F (149°C) on a candy thermometer. Remove from the heat.

As the syrup approaches temperature, beat the egg white in a heatproof stand-mixer bowl until stiff peaks form. With the mixer running, carefully pour the hot syrup into the egg white in a thin, steady stream down the side of the bowl, avoiding the whisk.
Beat until the mixture is thick, glossy, and beginning to hold its shape, about 5–8 minutes. Fold in the warm hazelnuts promptly with a sturdy spatula. The mixture will become stiff and sticky.
Scrape into the prepared pan and press into an even layer. Cover with the second wafer sheet, then a piece of parchment. Place a flat board on top and weight lightly to compact the nougat.

Leave at cool room temperature overnight to set. Lift out using the parchment, remove the parchment but leave the edible wafer in place, and cut into small pieces with a sturdy knife. Serve with the Christmas Eve Tió sweets.
tips: Use a candy thermometer: syrup temperature and humidity affect whether the nougat sets firm or chewy. Homemade texture may differ from artisan Torró d’Agramunt.
Work promptly once the nuts are added; an adult should handle the hot sugar syrup.
Keep tightly wrapped in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Avoid damp conditions, which make nougat sticky.
This hazelnut version contains nuts and egg.
